## Module Organization

The codebase is organized into functional modules, each responsible for a specific phase of the calculation pipeline. This separation of concerns enables maintainability and parallel development.

### Core Module Responsibilities

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Input Layer"
        CLP["commandlineparser.py<br/>parser<br/>Parse CLI arguments"]
        INP["input_parser.py<br/>input_file<br/>Parse mmpbsa.in"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Topology Layer"
        MAKETOP["make_top.py<br/>CheckMakeTop<br/>GROMACS → Amber topology"]
        PARMSETUP["parm_setup.py<br/>MMPBSA_System<br/>Map complex/receptor/ligand"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Trajectory Layer"
        MAKETRAJ["make_trajs.py<br/>Trajectory<br/>Strip, image, distribute frames"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Calculation Layer"
        CREATEIN["createinput.py<br/>SanderInput subclasses<br/>Generate .mdin files"]
        CALC["calculation.py<br/>CalculationList<br/>EnergyCalculation<br/>Execute sander/cpptraj"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Layer"
        AMBEROUT["amber_outputs.py<br/>AmberOutput subclasses<br/>Parse mdout files"]
        OUTFILE["output_file.py<br/>write_outputs()<br/>Format statistics"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Support Layer"
        UTILS["utils.py<br/>EnergyVector<br/>Helper functions"]
        TIMER["timer.py<br/>Timer<br/>Performance tracking"]
        EXCEPT["exceptions.py<br/>Custom exceptions"]
    end
    
    CLP --> MAKETOP
    INP --> CREATEIN
    MAKETOP --> PARMSETUP
    PARMSETUP --> MAKETRAJ
    MAKETRAJ --> CREATEIN
    CREATEIN --> CALC
    CALC --> AMBEROUT
    AMBEROUT --> OUTFILE
    
    UTILS -.supports.-> AMBEROUT
    TIMER -.supports.-> CALC
    EXCEPT -.used by.-> MAKETOP
    EXCEPT -.used by.-> CALC
```

**Sources**: [GMXMMPBSA/main.py:31-50](), [GMXMMPBSA/make_top.py:76-128](), [GMXMMPBSA/parm_setup.py:62-113](), [GMXMMPBSA/make_trajs.py:43-108](), [GMXMMPBSA/utils.py:52-63]()

### Module-to-Phase Mapping

| Phase | Primary Module | Key Classes/Functions | Purpose |
|-------|---------------|----------------------|---------|
| **Configuration** | `commandlineparser.py` | `parser` | Parse command-line arguments |
| | `input_parser.py` | `input_file` | Parse input file namelists |
| **Topology Generation** | `make_top.py` | `CheckMakeTop` | Convert GROMACS files to Amber format |
| | `parm_setup.py` | `MMPBSA_System`, `Residue` | Map complex to receptor/ligand |
| **Trajectory Preparation** | `make_trajs.py` | `Trajectory`, `make_trajectories()` | Strip solvent, distribute frames |
| **Input Generation** | `createinput.py` | `create_inputs()` | Generate calculation-specific `.mdin` files |
| **Calculation Execution** | `calculation.py` | `CalculationList`, `EnergyCalculation`, `NmodeCalc` | Run external programs, manage parallel execution |
| **Output Processing** | `amber_outputs.py` | `GBout`, `PBout`, `NMODEout`, `BindingStatistics` | Parse output files, compute statistics |
| | `output_file.py` | `write_outputs()`, `data2pkl()` | Format final results, serialize data |
| **Utilities** | `utils.py` | `EnergyVector`, helper functions | Data structures, common operations |

**Sources**: [GMXMMPBSA/main.py:1-50](), [GMXMMPBSA/app.py:40-112]()

---

## Pipeline Architecture

gmx_MMPBSA follows a strict sequential pipeline where each phase must complete before the next begins. The `MMPBSA_App` class enforces this ordering and manages state transitions.

### Complete Execution Pipeline

```mermaid
graph TB
    START["Application Start<br/>gmxmmpbsa()"]
    
    subgraph "Phase 1: Initialization"
        P1A["setup_run()<br/>Signal handlers"]
        P1B["MMPBSA_App.__init__()<br/>MPI, I/O, timers"]
        P1C["get_cl_args()<br/>commandlineparser.py"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Phase 2: Input Processing"
        P2A["read_input_file()<br/>input_parser.py"]
        P2B["process_input()<br/>Validate parameters"]
        P2C["check_for_bad_input()<br/>Sanity checks"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Phase 3: Topology Generation"
        P3A["make_prmtops()<br/>CheckMakeTop.buildTopology()"]
        P3B["gmx2pdb()<br/>Extract PDB from TPR/trajs"]
        P3C["gmxtop2prmtop() or pdb2prmtop()<br/>Convert to Amber format"]
        P3D["loadcheck_prmtops()<br/>MMPBSA_System.Map()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Phase 4: File Setup"
        P4A["file_setup()<br/>create_inputs()"]
        P4B["make_trajectories()<br/>Trajectory.Setup()"]
        P4C["cpptraj execution<br/>Strip, image, split frames"]
        P4D["make_mutant_trajectories()<br/>Alanine scanning"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Phase 5: Calculation"
        P5A["run_mmpbsa()<br/>load_calc_list()"]
        P5B["CalculationList.append()<br/>Build calculation sequence"]
        P5C["CalculationList.run()<br/>Execute all calculations"]
        P5D["Calculation.run()<br/>sander/cpptraj subprocess"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Phase 6: Output Processing"
        P6A["parse_output_files()<br/>AmberOutput classes"]
        P6B["Read mdout files<br/>Extract energies per frame"]
        P6C["Compute statistics<br/>Mean, SD, SEM"]
        P6D["write_final_outputs()<br/>FINAL_RESULTS_MMPBSA.dat"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Phase 7: Finalization"
        P7A["data2pkl()<br/>Serialize to .mmxsa"]
        P7B["finalize()<br/>Cleanup, timing report"]
    end
    
    START --> P1A
    P1A --> P1B
    P1B --> P1C
    P1C --> P2A
    P2A --> P2B
    P2B --> P2C
    P2C --> P3A
    P3A --> P3B
    P3B --> P3C
    P3C --> P3D
    P3D --> P4A
    P4A --> P4B
    P4B --> P4C
    P4C --> P4D
    P4D --> P5A
    P5A --> P5B
    P5B --> P5C
    P5C --> P5D
    P5D --> P6A
    P6A --> P6B
    P6B --> P6C
    P6C --> P6D
    P6D --> P7A
    P7A --> P7B
```

**Sources**: [GMXMMPBSA/app.py:40-112](), [GMXMMPBSA/main.py:65-210]()

### Phase-Specific Details

#### Phase 3: Topology Generation

This critical phase converts GROMACS topology files to Amber format:

```mermaid
graph TB
    TPR["GROMACS TPR/PDB files"]

    PDB2PRM["pdb2prmtop()<br/>Generate via tleap<br/>Line 127"]

    PRMTOP["COM.prmtop<br/>REC.prmtop<br/>LIG.prmtop"]
    
    MAPSYS["MMPBSA_System.Map()<br/>Map atoms to receptor/ligand<br/>Line 117"]
    
    TPR --> GMX2PDB
    TOP --> PATH1
    GMX2PDB --> PATH1
    
    PATH1 -->|Yes| GMXTOP
    PATH1 -->|No| PDB2PRM
    
    PDB2PRM --> TLEAP

```

**Critical Classes**:
- `CheckMakeTop`: Main topology generation orchestrator [GMXMMPBSA/make_top.py:76-144]()

## Key Data Structures

The `EnergyVector` is a NumPy array subclass that stores per-frame energies and provides automatic statistical methods:

```mermaid
graph TB

        VECTOR["EnergyVector(values, com_std)<br/>NumPy ndarray subclass"]
        
        METHODS["Statistical Methods:<br/>• mean() - Average<br/>• std() - Standard deviation<br/>• stdev() - Propagated SD<br/>• sem() - Standard error<br/>• semp() - Propagated SEM"]
        
        OPS["Arithmetic Operations:<br/>• __add__ - Propagate uncertainty<br/>• __sub__ - Propagate uncertainty<br/>• corr_add - Correlated addition<br/>• corr_sub - Correlated subtraction"]
    end
```

**Sources**: [GMXMMPBSA/utils.py:52-151]()

The `MMPBSA_System` class maintains the mapping between complex, receptor, and ligand topologies:


**Sources**: [GMXMMPBSA/parm_setup.py:33-113]()

---

## Summary

The gmx_MMPBSA internal architecture follows a strict pipeline design:

1. **MMPBSA_App** orchestrates the workflow [GMXMMPBSA/main.py:65]().
2. **CheckMakeTop** handles topology conversion [GMXMMPBSA/make_top.py:76]().
3. **Trajectory** class prepares frames via cpptraj [GMXMMPBSA/make_trajs.py:68]().
4. **EnergyVector** manages data and statistical propagation [GMXMMPBSA/utils.py:52]().

**Sources**: [GMXMMPBSA/main.py:65](), [GMXMMPBSA/make_top.py:76](), [GMXMMPBSA/make_trajs.py:43](), [GMXMMPBSA/utils.py:52]()

# Page: Error Handling and Exceptions

# Error Handling and Exceptions

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [GMXMMPBSA/API.py](GMXMMPBSA/API.py)
- [GMXMMPBSA/amber_outputs.py](GMXMMPBSA/amber_outputs.py)
- [GMXMMPBSA/calculation.py](GMXMMPBSA/calculation.py)
- [GMXMMPBSA/createinput.py](GMXMMPBSA/createinput.py)
- [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py](GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py)
- [GMXMMPBSA/input_parser.py](GMXMMPBSA/input_parser.py)
- [GMXMMPBSA/output_file.py](GMXMMPBSA/output_file.py)

</details>



This page documents the exception hierarchy, error handling patterns, and logging mechanisms used throughout gmx_MMPBSA. It explains how the system manages failures across serial and parallel execution modes, ensuring that errors are reported clearly and resources are cleaned up properly.

## Purpose and Scope

gmx_MMPBSA implements a comprehensive exception system for detecting and reporting errors during topology generation, trajectory processing, calculations, and output parsing. The system provides:

- A hierarchical exception structure with specialized error types [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:25-153]().
- MPI-aware error handling that coordinates across parallel processes [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:168-171]().
- Integration with the logging system for error tracking [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:170-170]().
- Graceful degradation and technical error reporting via the `GMXMMPBSA_ERROR` interface [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:168-172]().

---

## Exception Hierarchy

The following diagram shows the complete exception class hierarchy in gmx_MMPBSA:

**Exception Class Architecture**
```mermaid
graph TB
    Exception["Exception<br/>(Python built-in)"]
    Warning["Warning<br/>(Python built-in)"]
    
    MMPBSA_Error["MMPBSA_Error<br/>Base exception class"]
    MMPBSA_Warning["MMPBSA_Warning<br/>Base warning class"]
    
    TimerException["TimerException<br/>Timer errors"]
    CommandlineError["CommandlineError<br/>CLI parsing errors"]
    CalcError["CalcError<br/>Calculation failures"]
    SetupError["SetupError<br/>Environment setup errors"]
    PrmtopError["PrmtopError<br/>Topology file errors"]
    SelectionError["SelectionError<br/>Residue selection errors"]
    TrajError["TrajError<br/>Trajectory processing errors"]
    InputError["InputError<br/>Input file parsing errors"]
    IllegalOption["IllegalOption<br/>Incompatible options"]
    InterruptError["InterruptError<br/>Process interruption"]
    OutputError["OutputError<br/>Output parsing errors"]
    InconsistentError1["InconsistentError1<br/>Data inconsistency"]
    InconsistentError2["InconsistentError2<br/>Additional inconsistency"]
    LengthError["LengthError<br/>Array length mismatch"]
    DecompError["DecompError<br/>Decomposition errors"]
    MutantResError["MutantResError<br/>Mutation errors"]
    InternalError["InternalError<br/>Internal logic errors"]
    NoFileExists["NoFileExists<br/>File not found"]
    
    Exception --> MMPBSA_Error
    Warning --> MMPBSA_Warning
    
    MMPBSA_Error --> TimerException
    MMPBSA_Error --> CommandlineError
    MMPBSA_Error --> CalcError
    MMPBSA_Error --> SetupError
    MMPBSA_Error --> PrmtopError
    MMPBSA_Error --> SelectionError
    MMPBSA_Error --> TrajError
    MMPBSA_Error --> InputError
    MMPBSA_Error --> IllegalOption
    MMPBSA_Error --> InterruptError
    MMPBSA_Error --> OutputError
    MMPBSA_Error --> InconsistentError1
    MMPBSA_Error --> InconsistentError2
    MMPBSA_Error --> LengthError
    MMPBSA_Error --> DecompError
    MMPBSA_Error --> MutantResError
    MMPBSA_Error --> InternalError
    MMPBSA_Error --> NoFileExists
```
Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:25-153]()

---

## Exception Classes Reference

The following table summarizes all exception classes and their purposes:

| Exception Class | Purpose | Typical Use Cases |
|----------------|---------|-------------------|
| `MMPBSA_Error` | Base exception for all gmx_MMPBSA errors | Parent for all other exceptions [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:25-32]() |
| `MMPBSA_Warning` | Base warning class | Parent for non-fatal warnings [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:35-42]() |
| `TimerException` | Timer module errors | Failures in performance profiling [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:45-47]() |
| `CommandlineError` | Command-line parsing errors | Invalid flags or missing arguments [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:50-52]() |
| `CalcError` | Calculation execution failures | Sander/GBNSR6/cpptraj execution errors [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:55-57]() |
| `SetupError` | Environment setup issues | Missing external programs or invalid paths [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:60-62]() |
| `PrmtopError` | Topology file problems | Incompatible prmtop files [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:65-67]() |
| `SelectionError` | Invalid residue selections | Malformed masks [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:70-72]() |
| `TrajError` | Trajectory processing failures | Frame extraction errors [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:75-77]() |
| `InputError` | Input file parsing errors | Unrecognized namelists or invalid variables [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:80-82]() |
| `IllegalOption` | Incompatible option combinations | Conflicting calculation types [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:85-87]() |
| `InterruptError` | Process interruption | User cancellation (Ctrl+C) [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:90-92]() |
| `OutputError` | Output parsing failures | Malformed output files [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:95-97]() |
| `InconsistentError1` | Primary data inconsistency | Mismatched BOND, ANGLE, DIHED terms [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:100-104]() |
| `InconsistentError2` | Secondary inconsistency | Mismatched 1-4 VDW and 1-4 EEL terms [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:107-111]() |
| `LengthError` | Array length mismatches | Frame count inconsistencies in `EnergyVector` [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:134-138]() |
| `DecompError` | Decomposition analysis errors | Invalid decomposition results [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:141-143]() |
| `MutantResError` | Alanine scanning errors | Invalid mutation specifications [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:124-126]() |
| `InternalError` | Internal logic errors | Buggy coding or duplicate variables [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:146-148]() |
| `NoFileExists` | File not found | Missing required input/output files [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:151-153]() |

Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:25-153]()

---

## Error Handling Pattern: GMXMMPBSA_ERROR

The primary error handling mechanism is the `GMXMMPBSA_ERROR` class, which serves as a functional wrapper to provide centralized error logging and exception raising.

**Logic Flow of GMXMMPBSA_ERROR**
```mermaid
graph TB
    Start["GMXMMPBSA_ERROR<br/>instantiated"]
    Log["logging.error(msg)<br/>Writes to gmx_MMPBSA.log"]
    Raise["raise exc(msg)<br/>Stops execution"]
    
    Start --> Log
    Log --> Raise
```
Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:168-172]()

**Implementation Details:**
- **Centralized Logging**: The constructor immediately calls `logging.error()`, ensuring the error is recorded even if the exception is caught elsewhere [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:170]().
- **Traceability**: It prompts the user to check the `gmx_MMPBSA.log` file to report the problem [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:171]().
- **Type Flexibility**: It allows specifying the exception type (defaulting to `MMPBSA_Error`) [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:168]().

---

## Error Handling Workflow

The following diagram bridges the high-level system components with the specific code entities responsible for error management.

**Code Entity Error Flow**
```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Detection Points"
        Input["input_parser.py<br/>Variable.SetValue()"]
        Calc["calculation.py<br/>Calculation.run()"]
        Out["amber_outputs.py<br/>AmberOutput.summary_output()"]
        API["API.py<br/>_require_parquet_engine()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Error Handling"
        Wrapper["exceptions.py<br/>GMXMMPBSA_ERROR"]
        LogSys["logging module"]
    end
    
    Input -- "InputError" --> Wrapper
    Calc -- "CalcError" --> Wrapper
    Out -- "OutputError" --> Wrapper
    API -- "ImportError" --> LogSys
    
    Wrapper --> LogSys
    LogSys --> LogFile["gmx_MMPBSA.log"]
```
Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:168-172](), [GMXMMPBSA/calculation.py:163-164](), [GMXMMPBSA/amber_outputs.py:136-137](), [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:72-76]()

---

## Module-Specific Error Handling

### Input Parsing (input_parser.py)
The `Variable` and `Namelist` classes validate data types and structures during the initialization of the calculation parameters.

- **Variable Type Mismatch**: The `Variable` class checks if the provided `dat_type` is supported (int, str, float, list, tuple) [GMXMMPBSA/input_parser.py:41-44]().
- **Duplicate Variables**: The `Namelist.addVariable` method raises an `InternalError` if a variable is defined twice in the same namelist [GMXMMPBSA/input_parser.py:147-148]().
- **Namelist Integrity**: `Namelist.Open` prevents opening a namelist that is already open [GMXMMPBSA/input_parser.py:153-154]().

### Calculation Execution (calculation.py)
The calculation module ensures that the environment and external tools are ready before execution.

- **Setup Validation**: `MultiCalculation.run` checks the `calc_setup` flag. If `setup()` was not called, it raises a `CalcError` [GMXMMPBSA/calculation.py:163-164]().
- **Calculation List Integrity**: `CalculationList.append` ensures only `Calculation` or `MultiCalculation` instances are added, raising a `TypeError` otherwise [GMXMMPBSA/calculation.py:101-102]().

### Output Processing (amber_outputs.py)
The output system validates the state of data before generating reports.

- **Read State Check**: `AmberOutput.summary_output` and `AmberOutput.summary` verify that the output files have been successfully read (`is_read` flag) before attempting to format a summary [GMXMMPBSA/amber_outputs.py:136-137](), [GMXMMPBSA/amber_outputs.py:159-160]().

### API and Data Management (API.py)
The API module handles dependency and file system errors during post-processing.

- **Dependency Checks**: `_require_parquet_engine` raises an `ImportError` if neither `pyarrow` nor `fastparquet` is installed when disk-backed data is required [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:65-76]().
- **File Existence**: Functions using the API check for file presence, raising `NoFileExists` when expected results are missing [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:38]().

Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/input_parser.py:41-154](), [GMXMMPBSA/calculation.py:101-164](), [GMXMMPBSA/amber_outputs.py:136-160](), [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:65-76]()

---

## Logging System

gmx_MMPBSA uses the standard Python `logging` module to provide a consistent audit trail.

**Logging Components**
| Entity | Role | Code Reference |
|--------|------|----------------|
| `logging.error` | Records critical failures | [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:170]() |
| `GMXMMPBSA_INFO` | Handles standard information logging | [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:174-181]() |
| `logging.warning` | Reports non-fatal issues (e.g., setting `arad`) | [GMXMMPBSA/createinput.py:102]() |

**Data Flow in GMXMMPBSA_INFO:**
The `GMXMMPBSA_INFO` class takes a message and, via its `write` method, prints it to the console and writes it to the log file with an "INFO" prefix [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:178-180]().

Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:168-181](), [GMXMMPBSA/createinput.py:102-126]()

# Page: Parallel Processing and Performance

# Parallel Processing and Performance

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [GMXMMPBSA/analyzer/chartsettings.py](GMXMMPBSA/analyzer/chartsettings.py)
- [GMXMMPBSA/analyzer/customitem.py](GMXMMPBSA/analyzer/customitem.py)
- [GMXMMPBSA/analyzer/dialogs.py](GMXMMPBSA/analyzer/dialogs.py)
- [GMXMMPBSA/analyzer/gui.py](GMXMMPBSA/analyzer/gui.py)
- [GMXMMPBSA/analyzer/plots.py](GMXMMPBSA/analyzer/plots.py)
- [GMXMMPBSA/analyzer/utils.py](GMXMMPBSA/analyzer/utils.py)
- [GMXMMPBSA/fake_mpi.py](GMXMMPBSA/fake_mpi.py)
- [GMXMMPBSA/main.py](GMXMMPBSA/main.py)
- [GMXMMPBSA/make_top.py](GMXMMPBSA/make_top.py)
- [GMXMMPBSA/utils.py](GMXMMPBSA/utils.py)

</details>



This document describes the parallel processing architecture and performance optimization strategies in gmx_MMPBSA. It covers MPI-based frame parallelism in the calculation engine, multiprocessing in the analyzer application, and key performance considerations.

For information about the overall calculation workflow, see [Calculation Execution (3.3.3)](). For details about the analyzer application architecture, see [GUI Architecture and Components (4.1)]().

---

## Overview of Parallelization Strategy

gmx_MMPBSA employs two distinct parallelization approaches depending on the application:

1.  **MPI-based frame parallelism** in the core calculation engine (`gmx_MMPBSA`).
2.  **Multiprocessing/threading** in the analyzer GUI (`gmx_MMPBSA_ana`).

The fundamental design principle is **embarrassingly parallel frame processing**: each trajectory frame can be analyzed independently, enabling efficient distribution across compute resources without inter-process communication during calculation.

Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/main.py:72-110](), [GMXMMPBSA/fake_mpi.py:28-68]()

---

## MPI Frame Distribution Architecture

### Frame Distribution Strategy

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Master Process (Rank 0)"
        TRAJ["Input Trajectory<br/>N frames total"]
        CPPTRAJ["cpptraj Frame Extraction"]
        SPLIT["Frame Splitter"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Rank 0 Files"
        R0_TRJ["complex.nc.0<br/>frames: 0, mpi_size, 2*mpi_size..."]
        R0_INPCRD["_GMXMMPBSA_inpcrd_0/<br/>complexX.inpcrd"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Rank 1 Files"
        R1_TRJ["complex.nc.1<br/>frames: 1, mpi_size+1, 2*mpi_size+1..."]
        R1_INPCRD["_GMXMMPBSA_inpcrd_1/<br/>complexX.inpcrd"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Rank N-1 Files"
        RN_TRJ["complex.nc.N-1<br/>frames: N-1, mpi_size+N-1..."]
        RN_INPCRD["_GMXMMPBSA_inpcrd_N-1/<br/>complexX.inpcrd"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Parallel Calculation"
        CALC0["EnergyCalculation<br/>Rank 0<br/>sander/cpptraj"]
        CALC1["EnergyCalculation<br/>Rank 1<br/>sander/cpptraj"]
        CALCN["EnergyCalculation<br/>Rank N-1<br/>sander/cpptraj"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Collection"
        OUT0["complex_gb.mdout.0"]
        OUT1["complex_gb.mdout.1"]
        OUTN["complex_gb.mdout.N-1"]
        COLLECT["Master collects and parses"]
    end
    
    TRAJ --> CPPTRAJ
    CPPTRAJ --> SPLIT
    SPLIT --> R0_TRJ
    SPLIT --> R1_TRJ
    SPLIT --> RN_TRJ
    
    R0_TRJ --> CALC0
    R0_INPCRD --> CALC0
    R1_TRJ --> CALC1
    R1_INPCRD --> CALC1
    RN_TRJ --> CALCN
    RN_INPCRD --> CALCN
    
    CALC0 --> OUT0
    CALC1 --> OUT1
    CALCN --> OUTN
    
    OUT0 --> COLLECT
    OUT1 --> COLLECT
    OUTN --> COLLECT
```

The frame distribution follows a **round-robin pattern**: if `mpi_size = 4` and there are 100 frames, then:
*   Rank 0 processes frames: 0, 4, 8, 12, ..., 96
*   Rank 1 processes frames: 1, 5, 9, 13, ..., 97
*   Rank 2 processes frames: 2, 6, 10, 14, ..., 98
*   Rank 3 processes frames: 3, 7, 11, 15, ..., 99

This ensures balanced load distribution even if the total frame count is not evenly divisible by the number of ranks.

Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/make_trajs.py:52-181](), [GMXMMPBSA/main.py:133-151]()

### Trajectory Preparation and Frame Splitting

The `make_trajectories` function coordinates frame distribution. The `Trajectory` class (internal to `make_trajs.py`) constructs a `cpptraj` input script that outputs multiple trajectory files simultaneously using the `trajout` command combined with rank-specific frame selection.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Main as MMPBSA_App (main.py)
    participant MakeTraj as make_trajectories (make_trajs.py)
    participant cpptraj as cpptraj executable
    
    Main->>MakeTraj: make_trajectories(INPUT, FILES, mpi_size)
    Note over MakeTraj: Only master (rank 0) executes
    
    Note over MakeTraj: Setup cpptraj input script<br/>Strip solvent, autoimage
    
    loop For each MPI rank
        MakeTraj->>MakeTraj: Add "trajout complex.nc.{rank}<br/>onlyframes {rank+1},{rank+1+mpi_size},..."
    end
    
    MakeTraj->>cpptraj: Execute cpptraj
    cpptraj-->>MakeTraj: Generate complex.nc.0, complex.nc.1, ..., complex.nc.N-1
    
    Note over MakeTraj: Repeat for receptor and ligand
    
    MakeTraj-->>Main: Return (numframes, rec_frames, lig_frames, numframes_nmode)
```

Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/make_trajs.py:52-181](), [GMXMMPBSA/main.py:133-151]()

### MPI Synchronization Points

Key synchronization points ensure data integrity across the parallel workflow:
1.  **After trajectory preparation**: Ensures all ranks have access to split trajectory files before starting calculations [GMXMMPBSA/main.py:148]().
2.  **After mutation trajectories**: Synchronizes after mutant trajectory generation [GMXMMPBSA/main.py:161]().
3.  **Before output processing**: Ensures all calculations complete before the master aggregates results [GMXMMPBSA/main.py:209]().

Non-master ranks have their `stdout` redirected to `os.devnull` to prevent output clutter [GMXMMPBSA/main.py:96-97]().

Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/main.py:92-98](), [GMXMMPBSA/main.py:148](), [GMXMMPBSA/main.py:209]()

---

## Calculation Execution Model

### CalculationList Architecture

The `CalculationList` class in `GMXMMPBSA/calculation.py` orchestrates the parallel execution of various energy and entropy terms.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class CalculationList {
        +Timer timer
        +list output_files
        +int mpi_size
        +append(calc, label, timer_key, output_basename)
        +run(rank, stdout, stderr)
    }
    
    class Calculation {
        <<abstract>>
        +str program
        +str prmtop
        +run(rank, stdout, stderr)*
    }
    
    class EnergyCalculation {
        +str trajin
        +str mdin
        +str mdout
        +run(rank, stdout, stderr)
    }
    
    class ListEnergyCalculation {
        +list inpcrds
        +list mdouts
        +run(rank, stdout, stderr)
    }
    
    class NmodeCalc {
        +run(rank, stdout, stderr)
    }
    
    class InteractionEntropyCalc {
        +run(rank, stdout, stderr)
    }
    
    CalculationList o-- Calculation
    Calculation <|-- EnergyCalculation
    Calculation <|-- NmodeCalc
    Calculation <|-- InteractionEntropyCalc
    EnergyCalculation <|-- ListEnergyCalculation
```

Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/calculation.py:88-115](), [GMXMMPBSA/calculation.py:148-204]()

### Per-Frame vs Batch Calculation Patterns

*   **Standard Energy (GB/PB)**: Frames are processed sequentially within each rank using `sander` [GMXMMPBSA/calculation.py:148-204]().
*   **GBNSR6**: Uses `ListEnergyCalculation` to process a list of coordinate files (inpcrd) in batch [GMXMMPBSA/calculation.py:240-274]().
*   **Entropy (NMODE/QH)**: Each rank processes its assigned subset of frames in a single execution of the external program [GMXMMPBSA/calculation.py:365-430]().

### Progress Tracking

Progress is monitored via the `pb` function [GMXMMPBSA/calculation.py:53-86](), which runs in a separate thread. It scans output files (like `.mdout`) for completion markers (e.g., "FINAL RESULTS") to update a `tqdm` progress bar across all ranks.

Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/calculation.py:53-86](), [GMXMMPBSA/calculation.py:123-145]()

---

## Multiprocessing in the Analyzer

### Data Loading Parallelization

The analyzer GUI (`gmx_MMPBSA_ana`) uses a `multiprocessing.Pool` (or `ThreadPool`) during initialization to load multiple `.mmxsa` or info files concurrently.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Analyzer Main Process"
        GUI["GMX_MMPBSA_ANA (gui.py)"]
        DIALOG["InitDialog (dialogs.py)"]
        PROGRESS["ProcessingProgressBar"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Worker Processes"
        W1["Load System 1"]
        W2["Load System 2"]
        WN["Load System N"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Storage"
        RAM["Memory (DataFrames)"]
        DISK["Disk (Parquet Files)"]
    end
    
    GUI --> DIALOG
    DIALOG --> PROGRESS
    PROGRESS --> W1
    PROGRESS --> W2
    PROGRESS --> WN
    
    W1 --> RAM
    W1 --> DISK
    W2 --> RAM
    W2 --> DISK
```

Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/analyzer/dialogs.py:234-347](), [GMXMMPBSA/analyzer/gui.py:44-193]()

### Memory vs Disk Trade-off

Users can configure the analyzer to prioritize RAM or Disk space:
*   **In-Memory**: All data loaded into Pandas DataFrames. Faster chart rendering but high RAM usage [GMXMMPBSA/analyzer/dialogs.py:58-66]().
*   **On-Disk**: Data stored as temporary Parquet files. Slower due to I/O but handles massive datasets [GMXMMPBSA/analyzer/dialogs.py:68-84]().

---

## Performance Considerations

### Memory Management

*   **Calculation Engine**: Each rank only loads its frame subset. `EnergyVector` (a `numpy.ndarray` subclass) is used for efficient numerical storage and statistical operations [GMXMMPBSA/utils.py:52-151]().
*   **Analyzer**: Employs term thresholds to discard negligible energy contributions (default 0.01 kcal/mol) and non-contributing residues (default 0.5 kcal/mol) during loading to save memory [GMXMMPBSA/analyzer/dialogs.py:74-113]().

### Disk I/O Optimization

The system prefers NetCDF trajectories for faster I/O [GMXMMPBSA/main.py:251](). During MPI execution, each rank writes to its own set of output files (e.g., `_GMXMMPBSA_complex_gb.mdout.0`), avoiding file contention.

### Scaling Characteristics

*   **Optimal MPI Size**: Each rank should ideally process at least 5-10 frames. Using more ranks than frames results in idle resources.
*   **Setup Overhead**: Topology generation (`make_top.py`) and trajectory splitting (`make_trajs.py`) are performed by the master rank and do not scale with MPI size.

Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/main.py:133-151](), [GMXMMPBSA/timer.py:1-135]()

---

## Performance Monitoring

The `Timer` class tracks execution time for major phases: setup, cpptraj, and specific calculation types [GMXMMPBSA/timer.py:1-135](). These timings are reported in the final output and can be used to identify bottlenecks.

Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/timer.py:1-135](), [GMXMMPBSA/main.py:103-104]()

---

# Page: File Management and Temporary Files

# File Management and Temporary Files

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [GMXMMPBSA/infofile.py](GMXMMPBSA/infofile.py)
- [GMXMMPBSA/make_trajs.py](GMXMMPBSA/make_trajs.py)
- [GMXMMPBSA/parm_setup.py](GMXMMPBSA/parm_setup.py)
- [GMXMMPBSA/timer.py](GMXMMPBSA/timer.py)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This page documents gmx_MMPBSA's temporary file management system, including naming conventions, file categories, cleanup behavior, and storage strategies. Understanding this system is essential for debugging calculations, managing disk space, and recovering from interrupted runs.

For information about persistent output files (FINAL_RESULTS_*.dat, *.csv, etc.), see [Output Files and Data Formats](). For the state management system that enables checkpoint/resume, see [InfoFile]().

---

## Temporary File Prefix

All temporary files created by gmx_MMPBSA use a consistent prefix defined in the application:

```
_GMXMMPBSA_
```

This prefix serves multiple purposes:
- **Easy identification**: All intermediate files are immediately recognizable.
- **Cleanup safety**: Enables selective removal without affecting user files.
- **Namespace separation**: Prevents conflicts with user-provided files.

The prefix is set in `GMXMMPBSA/main.py` as `self.pre = '_GMXMMPBSA_'` and propagated throughout the application components.

**Sources**: [GMXMMPBSA/main.py:78-78](), [GMXMMPBSA/make_top.py:81-81]()

---

## File Categories and Lifecycle

### Overview of File Types

The following diagram maps the logical preparation phases to the specific code entities and file patterns generated during execution.

**Preparation to Code Entity Mapping**
```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Phase: Structure & Topology"
        A["gmx2pdb() / make_top.py"] -- generates --> B["_GMXMMPBSA_COM.pdb"]
        C["Topology Class / make_top.py"] -- generates --> D["COM.prmtop"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Phase: Trajectory Processing"
        E["make_trajectories() / make_trajs.py"] -- generates --> F["_GMXMMPBSA_complex.nc.{rank}"]
        E -- generates --> G["_GMXMMPBSA_complex.pdb"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Phase: Input Generation"
        H["create_inputs() / createinput.py"] -- generates --> I["_GMXMMPBSA_gb.mdin"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Phase: Execution"
        J["run() / calculation.py"] -- generates --> K["_GMXMMPBSA_complex_gb.mdout.{rank}"]
    end

    subgraph "Phase: State Management"
        L["write_info() / infofile.py"] -- generates --> M["_GMXMMPBSA_info"]
    end

    B --> D
    D --> I
    F --> J
    I --> J
    K --> L
```
**Sources**: [GMXMMPBSA/main.py:233-625](), [GMXMMPBSA/make_top.py:108-110](), [GMXMMPBSA/make_trajs.py:92-107](), [GMXMMPBSA/infofile.py:86-90]()

---

## Detailed File Categories

### 1. Structure Files
These PDB files contain extracted structures from GROMACS files, converted for Amber topology generation.

| File Pattern | Purpose | Created By | Cleanup |
|-------------|---------|------------|---------|
| `_GMXMMPBSA_COM.pdb` | Complex structure | `make_top.py:gmx2pdb()` | Optional |
| `_GMXMMPBSA_REC.pdb` | Receptor structure | `make_top.py:gmx2pdb()` | Optional |
| `_GMXMMPBSA_LIG.pdb` | Ligand structure | `make_top.py:gmx2pdb()` | Optional |

**Sources**: [GMXMMPBSA/make_top.py:263-526]()

### 2. Topology Files
Amber-format topology and coordinate files generated from GROMACS files.

| File Pattern | Purpose | Format | Cleanup |
|-------------|---------|--------|---------|
| `COM.prmtop` | Complex topology | Amber prmtop | Keep |
| `REC.prmtop` | Receptor topology | Amber prmtop | Keep |
| `LIG.prmtop` | Ligand topology | Amber prmtop | Keep |
| `MUT_*.prmtop` | Mutant topologies | Amber prmtop | Keep |

**Sources**: [GMXMMPBSA/make_top.py:562-608](), [GMXMMPBSA/make_top.py:575-591]()

### 3. Trajectory Files
Thread-specific trajectory files for parallel processing. The distribution is handled by the `Trajectory` class in `make_trajs.py`.

| File Pattern | Purpose | Format |
|-------------|---------|--------|
| `_GMXMMPBSA_complex.{fmt}.{rank}` | Per-thread complex frames | NetCDF (`nc`) or ASCII (`mdcrd`) |
| `_GMXMMPBSA_receptor.{fmt}.{rank}` | Per-thread receptor frames | NetCDF or ASCII |
| `_GMXMMPBSA_ligand.{fmt}.{rank}` | Per-thread ligand frames | NetCDF or ASCII |
| `_GMXMMPBSA_complex.pdb` | Reference structure (frame 1) | PDB |

**Sources**: [GMXMMPBSA/make_trajs.py:43-149](), [GMXMMPBSA/make_trajs.py:91-108]()

---

## Special: GBNSR6 Directories and GBNSR6 Calculation

GBNSR6 calculations require special file organization. Unlike standard GB/PB, GBNSR6 often involves individual frame processing in separate directories to manage `inpcrd` files for the numerical solver.

**GBNSR6 File Organization and Processing**
```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "make_trajs.py / make_trajectories()"
        A["Create Directory"] --> B["_GMXMMPBSA_inpcrd_{rank}/"]
        B --> C["Outtraj(..., filetype='restart')"]
    end

    subgraph "calculation.py / GBNSR6 Calculation"
        D["_GMXMMPBSA_inpcrd_{rank}/_GMXMMPBSA_complex.inpcrd"] -- input to --> E["gbnsr6 executable"]
        E -- generates --> F["_GMXMMPBSA_complex_gbnsr6.mdout"]
    end

    subgraph "Data Aggregation"
        F -- parsed by --> G["GBNSR6out Class"]
    end
```

In `make_trajs.py`, if `gbnsr6run` is active, a temporary directory is created for each rank to hold individual coordinate files:
- `_GMXMMPBSA_inpcrd_{rank}/` [GMXMMPBSA/make_trajs.py:104-105]()
- `_GMXMMPBSA_inpcrd_{rank}/{pre}complex.inpcrd` [GMXMMPBSA/make_trajs.py:106-107]()

**Sources**: [GMXMMPBSA/make_trajs.py:103-107](), [GMXMMPBSA/calculation.py:202-202]()

---

## Cleanup Options and Behavior

### The `keep_files` Parameter
The `keep_files` input parameter controls temporary file retention. It is parsed from the `&general` namelist.

| Value | Behavior | Use Case |
|-------|----------|----------|
| `0` | Remove temporary files after completion | Production runs (default) |
| `1` | Keep temporary files in working directory | Debugging, inspection |
| `2` | Keep files in `_GMXMMPBSA_{sys_name}/` subdirectory | Organized archiving |

### Files Always Retained
Regardless of the `keep_files` setting, these files are essential for post-processing and state recovery:
- `_GMXMMPBSA_info`: Written by `InfoFile.write_info()`. Contains the serialized state of `INPUT` and `FILES`. [GMXMMPBSA/infofile.py:86-113]()
- `FINAL_RESULTS_MMPBSA.dat`: The primary statistics output.
- `*.prmtop`: Amber topologies generated during setup.

**Sources**: [GMXMMPBSA/infofile.py:86-113](), [GMXMMPBSA/main.py:78-78]()

---

## MPI-Specific File Handling

### Rank-Based File Distribution
In MPI mode, the `make_trajectories` function calculates the frames assigned to each rank to ensure balanced workloads.

```python
# Frame distribution logic in make_trajs.py
frames_per_rank = traj.processed_frames // size
extras = traj.processed_frames - frames_per_rank * size
frame_count = [frames_per_rank for i in range(size)]
for i in range(size):
    if i < extras: frame_count[i] += 1
```
[GMXMMPBSA/make_trajs.py:84-88]()

Each rank `i` then generates its own trajectory segment named `_GMXMMPBSA_complex.nc.i`. [GMXMMPBSA/make_trajs.py:100-101]()

**Sources**: [GMXMMPBSA/make_trajs.py:84-108]()

---

## Performance Profiling: Timer
The `Timer` class in `timer.py` tracks the duration of various phases. While not a "file" in the traditional sense, it outputs timing data to the log file.

- **Global Timer**: Tracks total execution time. [GMXMMPBSA/timer.py:35-35]()
- **Units**: Automatically scales from seconds to minutes, hours, or days based on duration. [GMXMMPBSA/timer.py:106-114]()

**Sources**: [GMXMMPBSA/timer.py:27-128]()

---

## Summary of File Naming Patterns

| Component | Pattern | Variable Reference |
|-----------|---------|--------------------|
| **Prefix** | `_GMXMMPBSA_` | `self.pre` in `main.py` |
| **Trajectory** | `{pre}complex.{ext}.{rank}` | `trj_suffix` in `make_trajs.py` |
| **Info File** | `{pre}info` | `name` in `infofile.py` |
| **GBNSR6 Dir** | `{pre}inpcrd_{rank}` | `temp_dir` in `make_trajs.py` |

**Sources**: [GMXMMPBSA/main.py:78-78](), [GMXMMPBSA/make_trajs.py:52-104](), [GMXMMPBSA/infofile.py:89-89]()

# Page: API Reference (MMPBSA_API)

# API Reference (MMPBSA_API)

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [GMXMMPBSA/API.py](GMXMMPBSA/API.py)
- [GMXMMPBSA/amber_outputs.py](GMXMMPBSA/amber_outputs.py)
- [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py](GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py)
- [GMXMMPBSA/output_file.py](GMXMMPBSA/output_file.py)
- [docs/analyzer.md](docs/analyzer.md)
- [docs/api.md](docs/api.md)
- [docs/examples/API/README.md](docs/examples/API/README.md)
- [docs/howworks.md](docs/howworks.md)
- [examples/API/COMPACT_MMXSA_RESULTS.mmxsa](examples/API/COMPACT_MMXSA_RESULTS.mmxsa)
- [examples/API/README.md](examples/API/README.md)
- [examples/API/extract_api_data.py](examples/API/extract_api_data.py)
- [examples/API/gb_delta_total.csv](examples/API/gb_delta_total.csv)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This document provides technical reference for the `MMPBSA_API` class and the high-level `API` module, which enable programmatic access to `gmx_MMPBSA` calculation results. The API allows custom Python scripts to load, filter, and analyze energy data, entropy calculations, and decomposition results without rerunning calculations. It exposes the free energy data (optionally to numpy arrays) so that users can leverage the full power of Python's scientific extensions (e.g., `numpy`, `scipy`, `pandas`) [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:1-6]().

**Related Documentation:**
- For command-line result analysis, see [Analyzer Application (gmx_MMPBSA_ana)](#4)
- For output file formats, see [Output Files and Data Formats](#5)
- For calculation setup, see [Core Application (gmx_MMPBSA)](#3)

Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:1-6]().

---

## Overview

The `MMPBSA_API` class provides a high-level interface for loading `gmx_MMPBSA` results from either binary `.mmxsa` files or calculation directories. It exposes energy data as pandas DataFrames, enabling custom statistical analysis, visualization, and data manipulation.

**Key Capabilities:**
- Load results from completed calculations via `load()` or `MMPBSA_API.load_file()` [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:230-252]().
- Filter data by calculation type, energy model, molecule, and energy term [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:294-315]().
- Access raw per-frame energies or statistical summaries [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:87-108]().
- Retrieve entropy calculations (NMODE, QH, IE, C2) [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:411-440]().
- Process decomposition analysis data [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:1050-1070]().
- Handle both normal and mutant calculations [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:1354-1370]().

Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:230-1370]().

---

## Basic Usage Workflow

### Natural Language to Code Entity Mapping: Initialization and Loading

| System Name | Code Entity | File Reference |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| High-level Loader | `GMXMMPBSA.API.load` | [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:1444-1454]() |
| Core API Class | `GMXMMPBSA.API.MMPBSA_API` | [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:195-200]() |
| Result Metadata | `get_info()` | [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:253-259]() |
| Input Parameters | `get_input()` | [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:261-268]() |
| Energy Data | `get_energy()` | [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:294-315]() |

Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:195-1454]().

### API Usage Pattern

The recommended way to load data in modern versions of `gmx_MMPBSA` is using the `load()` function in the `API` module.

```python
from GMXMMPBSA import API

# Load from a compact binary file
api = API.load("COMPACT_MMXSA_RESULTS.mmxsa")

# Get metadata
input_settings = api.get_input()
calculation_info = api.get_info()

# Retrieve energy data (e.g. GB binding energy)
# Returns (map, data, summary, component_summary)
_, energy_data, summary, _ = api.get_energy(model='gb', mol='delta')

# Access delta energy DataFrame
gb_delta_df = energy_data['normal']['gb']
print(summary['normal']['gb'])
```

Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:1444-1454](), [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:253-315]().

---

## Data Loading and Serialization

### File Format Support

The API supports two primary input formats:
1. **Info Files (`_GMXMMPBSA_info`)**: A text-based metadata file that points to external calculation outputs [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:230-252]().
2. **Compact Binary (`.mmxsa`)**: A serialized pickle file containing the entire result payload [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:1031-1048]().

### Compact Result Generation
The compact `.mmxsa` file is generated at the end of a calculation by the `data2pkl` function. It stores the `INPUT` namelists, `FILES` namespace, frame counts, and calculation types [GMXMMPBSA/output_file.py:31-51]().

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Output Generation"
        APP["Calculation App"] --> D2PKL["data2pkl()"]
        D2PKL --> MMXSA["COMPACT_MMXSA_RESULTS.mmxsa"]
    end
    
    subgraph "API Loading"
        MMXSA --> LOAD["API.load()"]
        LOAD --> BINARY["_get_fromBinary()"]
        BINARY --> API_OBJ["MMPBSA_API Object"]
    end
```
Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/output_file.py:31-51](), [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:1031-1048]().

---

## Energy and Entropy Data Structures

### Result Types and Components

The API organizes data into hierarchical keys based on the calculation context.

| Category | Keys | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Result Type** | `normal`, `mutant`, `mutant-normal` | Original, mutated (alanine scan), or difference [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:322-328]() |
| **Molecule** | `complex`, `receptor`, `ligand`, `delta` | Component or binding difference [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:334-338]() |
| **Energy Terms** | `BOND`, `VDWAALS`, `EEL`, `EGB`, `EPB`, etc. | Individual physical components [GMXMMPBSA/amber_outputs.py:44-62]() |

Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:322-338](), [GMXMMPBSA/amber_outputs.py:44-62]().

### The EnergyVector System
All per-frame energy data is stored in `EnergyVector` objects, which are specialized list derivatives designed for statistical operations on molecular dynamics frames [GMXMMPBSA/amber_outputs.py:105-107]().

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class EnergyVector {
        +ndarray data
        +mean()
        +std()
        +sem()
        +corr_add(other)
        +corr_sub(other)
    }
    class AmberOutput {
        +dict data_keys
        +EnergyVector BOND
        +EnergyVector EEL
        +EnergyVector TOTAL
        +summary()
    }
    AmberOutput "1" *-- "many" EnergyVector : contains
```
Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/amber_outputs.py:105-107](), [GMXMMPBSA/utils.py:52-151]().

---

## Technical Reference: Methods

### get_energy()
Retrieves energy calculations with extensive filtering and frame range selection [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:294-315]().

**Signature:**
```python
def get_energy(etype=None, model=None, mol=None, term=None, 
               remove_empty_terms=True, threshold=0.01, 
               startframe=None, endframe=None, interval=1)
```

**Return Structure:**
- `map`: Dictionary of available keys [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:397]()
- `data`: Nested dictionary of pandas DataFrames (per-frame values) [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:399]()
- `summary`: Statistical summaries (Average, SD, SEM) [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:401]()

Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:294-409]().

### get_entropy()
Retrieves entropy results for `nmode`, `qh`, `ie` (Interaction Entropy), or `c2` [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:411-440]().

**Method Keys:**
- `nmode`: Normal Mode Analysis [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:454]()
- `qh`: Quasi-Harmonic [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:454]()
- `ie`: Interaction Entropy [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:458]()
- `c2`: C2 Entropy [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:465]()

Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:411-476]().

### get_decomp_energy()
Accesses decomposition data. This method handles the complex multi-indexing required for per-residue and pairwise analysis [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:1050-1070]().

**Residue Naming:**
Residues are identified using the format `MOL:CHAIN:RESNAME:RESNUM` (e.g., `R:A:ARG:10`) [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:1145-1150]().

Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:1050-1150]().

---

## Data Management and Performance

The API provides options to handle large datasets (e.g., 200,000+ frames) by offloading data to disk [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:135-158]().

| Setting | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `inmemory` | `False` | If True, stores DataFrames in RAM. If False, uses Parquet files [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:135-140]() |
| `temp_path` | `Path` | Location for temporary Parquet files [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:136]() |

### Performance Optimization
`gmx_MMPBSA_ana` and the API were optimized in version 1.5.5 to improve data processing speeds significantly (up to 265x for large energy datasets) by:
- Implementing multithreading for data processing [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:31]()
- Optimizing access to subsets in pandas DataFrames [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:173-175]()
- Using disk-backed storage via Parquet engines (`pyarrow` or `fastparquet`) [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:65-76]()

Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:31-158](), [docs/analyzer.md:21-45]().

---

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "API Module (GMXMMPBSA/API.py)"
        LOAD["load()"]

    end
    
    subgraph "Output Processing (GMXMMPBSA/amber_outputs.py)"
        AOUT["class AmberOutput"]
        NOUT["class NMODEout"]
        IEOUT["class IEout"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Storage (GMXMMPBSA/utils.py)"
        EVEC["class EnergyVector"]
    end

    LOAD --> MAPI
    MAPI -- parses --> AOUT
    MAPI -- parses --> NOUT
    MAPI -- parses --> IEOUT
    AOUT -- stores --> EVEC
```

Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:1-1454](), [GMXMMPBSA/amber_outputs.py:65-108](), [GMXMMPBSA/utils.py:52-60]().

This guide provides technical documentation for developers who want to contribute to, extend, or deeply understand the gmx_MMPBSA codebase. It covers the internal architecture, development workflows, and implementation details necessary for working with the source code.

For end-user documentation on running gmx_MMPBSA, see [Core Application (gmx_MMPBSA)](#3). For information on using the API to access calculation results programmatically, see [API Reference (MMPBSA_API)](#7.5). For testing your installation, see [Validation with gmx_MMPBSA_test](#2.2).

---

## Repository Organization

The gmx_MMPBSA repository follows a standard Python package structure with distinct directories for source code, documentation, tests, and examples. The project requires Python 3.11 as specified in the build configuration [setup.py:26-27]().

**Directory Structure**

```mermaid
graph TB
    ROOT["gmx_MMPBSA/<br/>(repository root)"]
    
    ROOT --> GMXMMPBSA["GMXMMPBSA/<br/>(main package)"]
    ROOT --> DOCS["docs/<br/>(MkDocs documentation)"]
    ROOT --> EXAMPLES["examples/<br/>(test systems)"]
    ROOT --> SETUP["setup.py<br/>(distribution config)"]
    ROOT --> VERS["versioneer.py<br/>(version management)"]
    ROOT --> CFG["setup.cfg<br/>(versioneer config)"]
    
    GMXMMPBSA --> CORE["Core Modules:<br/>main.py<br/>calculation.py<br/>amber_outputs.py"]
    GMXMMPBSA --> APP["app.py<br/>(entry points)"]
    GMXMMPBSA --> VER["_version.py<br/>(git versioning)"]
    GMXMMPBSA --> ANALYZER["analyzer/<br/>(GUI application)"]
    GMXMMPBSA --> DATA["data/<br/>(parameter files)"]
    
    EXAMPLES --> SYSTEMS["System types:<br/>Protein_ligand/<br/>Protein_protein/<br/>etc."]
```

**Key Files and Their Roles**

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `GMXMMPBSA/app.py` | Console script entry points: `gmxmmpbsa()`, `gmxmmpbsa_ana()`, `gmxmmpbsa_test()` [GMXMMPBSA/app.py:116-168]() |
| `setup.py` | Package metadata, dependencies (numpy, pandas, etc.), and console script registration [setup.py:29-62]() |
| `versioneer.py` | Tool for managing recorded version numbers in setuptools-based projects [versioneer.py:17-21]() |
| `GMXMMPBSA/_version.py` | Git implementation for computing version numbers from source trees [GMXMMPBSA/_version.py:12-13]() |
| `GMXMMPBSA/data/` | Force field parameter files, xvv files for RISM, and GUI styles [setup.py:34]() |

Sources: [setup.py:26-62](), [GMXMMPBSA/app.py:116-168](), [versioneer.py:1-21](), [GMXMMPBSA/_version.py:1-60]()

---

## Application Architecture

gmx_MMPBSA consists of three independent console applications that share common library code but serve distinct purposes. These are registered as entry points in the package configuration [setup.py:56-61]().

**Three-Application System**

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Console Scripts (setup.py:56-61)"
        MAIN["gmx_MMPBSA<br/>Entry: app.gmxmmpbsa"]
        ANA["gmx_MMPBSA_ana<br/>Entry: app.gmxmmpbsa_ana"]
        TEST["gmx_MMPBSA_test<br/>Entry: app.gmxmmpbsa_test"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Application Logic (GMXMMPBSA/app.py)"
        BASE["_gmxmmpbsa_base<br/>Initializes MPI, Logging,<br/>and MMPBSA_App"]
        RUNTEST["run_test<br/>Executes test suite"]
        GUISTART["GMX_MMPBSA_ANA<br/>Launches PyQt interface"]
    end
    
    subgraph "External Integrations"
        MPI4PY["mpi4py<br/>Parallel execution"]
        PYQT["PyQt5/PyQt6<br/>GUI framework"]
        VERS["versioneer<br/>Version retrieval"]
    end
    
    MAIN --> BASE
    ANA --> GUISTART
    TEST --> RUNTEST
    
    BASE --> MPI4PY
    GUISTART --> PYQT
    MAIN -.version.-> VERS
```

**Execution Entry Points**

The primary entry points are defined in `GMXMMPBSA/app.py`:
- `gmxmmpbsa()`: The main calculation engine [GMXMMPBSA/app.py:116-118]().
- `gmxmmpbsa_ana()`: The GUI analyzer, requiring PyQt5 or PyQt6 [GMXMMPBSA/app.py:123-151]().
- `gmxmmpbsa_test()`: The testing utility [GMXMMPBSA/app.py:154-168]().

Sources: [setup.py:56-61](), [GMXMMPBSA/app.py:40-168](), [GMXMMPBSA/__init__.py:24-35]()

---

## Build and Distribution System

The project uses `versioneer` to handle versioning automatically based on Git tags. This ensures that the version string in `GMXMMPBSA.__version__` is always synchronized with the repository state [GMXMMPBSA/__init__.py:34-35]().

**Versioning and Setup Configuration**

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Build Config"
        SETUP["setup.py"]
        CFG["setup.cfg"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Versioneer System"
        VERS["versioneer.py"]
        V_PY["GMXMMPBSA/_version.py"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Package Metadata"
        INIT["GMXMMPBSA/__init__.py"]
    end
    
    SETUP -- uses --> VERS
    VERS -- generates --> V_PY
    CFG -- configures --> VERS
    INIT -- imports --> V_PY
```

**Key Distribution Components**
- **Dependency Management**: Dependencies like `numpy==1.26.4`, `pandas==1.5.3`, and `mpi4py==4.0.1` are strictly pinned or ranged in `setup.py` [setup.py:50-55]().
- **Versioneer Config**: `setup.cfg` defines the version file source and tag prefix [setup.cfg:1-7]().
- **Manifest**: `MANIFEST.in` ensures `versioneer.py` and `_version.py` are included in source distributions [MANIFEST.in:1-3]().

Sources: [setup.py:29-62](), [setup.cfg:1-7](), [versioneer.py:98-113](), [GMXMMPBSA/_version.py:47-59]()

# Project Structure

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

This page provides an overview of the gmx_MMPBSA repository organization, package structure, and key modules. It serves as a map for developers who want to understand how the codebase is organized and where to find specific functionality.

For information about building and distributing the package, see [8.2 Building and Distribution](). For details about the documentation system, see [8.3 Documentation System]().

## Repository Layout

The gmx_MMPBSA repository follows a standard Python package structure with setuptools-based installation. It requires Python 3.11 [setup.py:26-27]().

```
gmx_MMPBSA/
├── GMXMMPBSA/              # Main package directory
│   ├── __init__.py         # Package metadata and exports
│   ├── app.py              # Application entry points and CLI logic
│   ├── main.py             # Core application orchestration (MMPBSA_App)
│   ├── commandlineparser.py# Argument parsing for all apps
│   ├── input_parser.py     # mmpbsa.in parsing and validation
│   ├── make_top.py         # GROMACS to AMBER topology conversion
│   ├── make_trajs.py       # Trajectory processing and MPI distribution
│   ├── calculation.py      # Execution of sander/cpptraj/nmode
│   ├── createinput.py      # Generation of .mdin and .in files
│   ├── amber_outputs.py    # Parsers for AMBER output files
│   ├── output_file.py      # Result writing (DAT, CSV, MMXSA)
│   ├── parm_setup.py       # Topology manipulation and masking
│   ├── utils.py            # EnergyVector and common utilities
│   ├── API.py              # Programmatic API (MMPBSA_API)
│   ├── timer.py            # Performance profiling
│   ├── infofile.py         # State management and checkpoints
│   ├── exceptions.py       # Custom exception hierarchy
│   ├── tester.py           # Logic for gmx_MMPBSA_test
│   ├── analyzer/           # GUI analyzer source code
│   │   ├── gui.py          # Main PyQt window
│   │   ├── utils.py        # GUI data loading
│   │   └── style/          # CSS stylesheets
│   └── data/               # XVV files and template data
├── setup.py                # Installation and dependency config
├── setup.cfg               # Versioneer configuration
├── versioneer.py           # Git-based versioning script
└── MANIFEST.in             # Package distribution manifest
```

**Sources:** [setup.py:29-62](), [GMXMMPBSA/__init__.py:24-35](), [MANIFEST.in:1-3](), [setup.cfg:1-7]()

## Console Script Entry Points

The package registers four console scripts that become available system-wide after installation via the `entry_points` configuration in `setup.py` [setup.py:56-61]().

| Script Name | Entry Point Function | Module | Purpose |
|------------|-------------------|---------------|---------|
| `gmx_MMPBSA` | `gmxmmpbsa` | `GMXMMPBSA.app` | Main calculation driver for GROMACS files |
| `amber_MMPBSA` | `gmxmmpbsa_amber` | `GMXMMPBSA.app` | Calculation driver for AMBER files |
| `gmx_MMPBSA_ana` | `gmxmmpbsa_ana` | `GMXMMPBSA.app` | GUI analyzer for result visualization |
| `gmx_MMPBSA_test` | `gmxmmpbsa_test` | `GMXMMPBSA.app` | Installation validation utility |

**Sources:** [setup.py:56-61](), [GMXMMPBSA/app.py:116-168]()

## Core Application Module Hierarchy

The following diagram illustrates the relationship between the main entry point and the functional modules during a calculation run.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Application Entry"
        APP_PY["app.py<br/>_gmxmmpbsa_base()"]
        MAIN_PY["main.py<br/>MMPBSA_App"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Configuration Layer"
        CLPARSER["commandlineparser.py<br/>parser / anaparser / testparser"]
        INPARSER["input_parser.py<br/>InputFile / Namelist"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Topology & Trajectory Pipeline"
        MAKETOP["make_top.py<br/>CheckMakeTop"]
        PARMSETUP["parm_setup.py<br/>MMPBSA_System"]
        MAKETRAJ["make_trajs.py<br/>Trajectory"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Execution Layer"
        CREATEINPUT["createinput.py<br/>SanderInput subclasses"]
        CALC["calculation.py<br/>CalculationList / EnergyCalculation"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Processing"
        AMBEROUT["amber_outputs.py<br/>AmberOutput / BindingStatistics"]
        OUTFILE["output_file.py<br/>write_outputs() / data2pkl()"]

    end

    APP_PY --> MAIN_PY
    MAIN_PY --> CLPARSER
    MAIN_PY --> INPARSER
    MAIN_PY --> MAKETOP
    MAKETOP --> PARMSETUP
    MAIN_PY --> MAKETRAJ
    MAIN_PY --> CREATEINPUT
    MAIN_PY --> CALC
    CALC --> AMBEROUT
    AMBEROUT --> OUTFILE
    MAIN_PY --> INFO
```

**Sources:** [GMXMMPBSA/app.py:40-113](), [GMXMMPBSA/__init__.py:24-26]()

## Module-by-Module Breakdown

### Entry Point and Orchestration

#### `app.py` - CLI Wrapper
This module handles the initial logging setup, MPI initialization (using `mpi4py` or a `fake_mpi` fallback for serial runs), and directs execution to the appropriate sub-application [GMXMMPBSA/app.py:40-55]().

**Key Functions:**
- `_gmxmmpbsa_base(parser, engine)`: The core logic shared by `gmx_MMPBSA` and `amber_MMPBSA`. It instantiates `MMPBSA_App` and calls the high-level workflow methods [GMXMMPBSA/app.py:40-113]().
- `gmxmmpbsa_ana()`: Initializes the `QApplication` and launches the GUI analyzer [GMXMMPBSA/app.py:123-151]().
- `gmxmmpbsa_test()`: Launches the automated testing suite [GMXMMPBSA/app.py:154-168]().

#### `main.py` - Core Logic Orchestrator
**Primary Class:** `MMPBSA_App`
The `MMPBSA_App` class coordinates the sequential steps of the calculation. It is responsible for calling `make_prmtops()`, `file_setup()`, and `run_mmpbsa()` in the correct order [GMXMMPBSA/app.py:90-103]().

**Sources:** [GMXMMPBSA/app.py:40-168]()

### Calculation Subsystems

#### `calculation.py` - Execution Engine
This module contains the `CalculationList` class, which manages a collection of `Calculation` objects (e.g., `EnergyCalculation`, `NmodeCalc`). It handles the execution of external tools like `sander`, `cpptraj`, and `mmpbsa_py_energy` [GMXMMPBSA/__init__.py:24-26]().

#### `amber_outputs.py` - Result Parsing
Contains classes designed to parse the text-based output files from AMBER.
- `AmberOutput`: Base class for all parsers.
- `BindingStatistics`: Aggregates parsed data to calculate final binding free energies and statistical uncertainties [GMXMMPBSA/__init__.py:24-26]().

**Sources:** [GMXMMPBSA/__init__.py:24-26](), [GMXMMPBSA/app.py:111-112]()

### GUI Analyzer

#### `analyzer/gui.py`
The entry point for the visual analysis tool. It uses `PyQt6` (or `PyQt5` as fallback) to provide a multi-document interface (MDI) for exploring energy components, residue decomposition, and correlations [GMXMMPBSA/app.py:125-149]().

**Sources:** [GMXMMPBSA/app.py:123-151]()

## Data Flow: From CLI to Results

The following diagram maps the internal data flow from the command line interface through the internal data structures to the final output files.

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Input Space"
        CLI["sys.argv"]
        IN_FILE["mmpbsa.in"]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        PARSER["commandlineparser.py<br/>parser.parse_args()"]
        IN_OBJ["input_parser.py<br/>InputFile()"]
        APP_OBJ["main.py<br/>MMPBSA_App"]
        CALC_LIST["calculation.py<br/>CalculationList"]
    end

    subgraph "Output Space"
        INFO_FILE["_GMXMMPBSA_info"]
        DAT_FILE["FINAL_RESULTS_MMPBSA.dat"]
        MMXSA["COMPACT_RESULTS.mmxsa"]
    end

    CLI --> PARSER
    IN_FILE --> IN_OBJ
    PARSER --> APP_OBJ
    IN_OBJ --> APP_OBJ
    APP_OBJ --> CALC_LIST
    APP_OBJ --> INFO_FILE
    CALC_LIST --> DAT_FILE
    APP_OBJ --> MMXSA
```

**Sources:** [GMXMMPBSA/app.py:65-113](), [GMXMMPBSA/infofile.py:26](), [GMXMMPBSA/output_file.py:31-52]()

## Versioning System

The project uses `versioneer` to manage version strings dynamically based on Git tags. This ensures that the version reported by the tool always matches the repository state [setup.py:20-32]().

- **Configuration**: Defined in `setup.cfg` under the `[versioneer]` section [setup.cfg:1-7]().
- **Source**: `GMXMMPBSA/_version.py` is the generated file containing the version metadata [GMXMMPBSA/_version.py:1-60]().
- **Integration**: `setup.py` calls `versioneer.get_version()` to set the package version during build/install [setup.py:31]().

**Sources:** [setup.py:20-32](), [setup.cfg:1-7](), [GMXMMPBSA/_version.py:1-60](), [versioneer.py:1-125]()

This page documents the build configuration, version management, and distribution mechanisms for gmx_MMPBSA. It covers how the package is configured for installation, how versions are managed, and the various channels through which users can obtain the software. For information about the project's file organization, see [Project Structure](#8.1). For details on the documentation build system, see [Documentation System](#8.3).

## Package Configuration Overview

The gmx_MMPBSA package is built using Python's standard `setuptools` infrastructure, with enhanced version management provided by `versioneer`. The build configuration enforces strict dependency requirements to ensure compatibility across the AmberTools and GROMACS ecosystems.

### setup.py Structure

```mermaid
graph TB
    SETUP["setup.py<br/>Main configuration"]
    VERSION["versioneer<br/>Git-based versioning"]
    METADATA["Package Metadata<br/>name, author, license"]
    DEPS["install_requires<br/>Pinned dependencies"]
    PKGS["find_packages()<br/>Auto-discovery"]
    DATA["package_data<br/>Non-Python resources"]
    ENTRY["entry_points<br/>Console scripts"]
    
    SETUP --> VERSION
    SETUP --> METADATA
    SETUP --> DEPS
    SETUP --> PKGS
    SETUP --> DATA
    SETUP --> ENTRY
    
    VERSION --> VERSION_STR["version string<br/>from git tags"]
    VERSION --> CMDCLASS["cmdclass<br/>build commands"]
    
    DEPS --> NUMPY["numpy==1.26.4"]
    DEPS --> PANDAS["pandas==1.5.3"]
    DEPS --> MPT["matplotlib==3.7.3"]
    DEPS --> MPI["mpi4py==4.0.1"]
    DEPS --> PARMED["parmed>=4.2.2"]
    DEPS --> OTHERS["scipy, seaborn, tqdm"]
    
    DATA --> DATAFILES["data/*"]
    DATA --> STYLES["analyzer/style/*"]
    DATA --> BASH["GMXMMPBSA.sh"]
    
    ENTRY --> MAIN["gmx_MMPBSA"]
    ENTRY --> AMBER["amber_MMPBSA"]
    ENTRY --> ANA["gmx_MMPBSA_ana"]
    ENTRY --> TEST["gmx_MMPBSA_test"]
```

Sources: [setup.py:19-62]()

The [setup.py:29-62]() file contains the complete package configuration. Key components include:

| Configuration Element | Purpose | Location |
|----------------------|---------|----------|
| Package discovery | Automatic discovery of Python packages | [setup.py:33]() |
| Version management | Git-based versioning via versioneer | [setup.py:31-32]() |
| Dependencies | Pinned scientific stack versions | [setup.py:50-55]() |
| Console scripts | Four command-line entry points | [setup.py:56-61]() |
| Package data | Non-Python resources (data files, styles) | [setup.py:34]() |

## Python Version Enforcement

gmx_MMPBSA strictly requires Python 3.11. This requirement is enforced at installation time:

```python
# From setup.py
if sys.version_info[:2] != (3, 11):
    raise RuntimeError("gmx_MMPBSA requires python == 3.11")
```

Sources: [setup.py:26-27]()

This strict enforcement prevents installation with incompatible Python versions, ensuring consistent behavior across all deployments. The requirement is specified as an exact match for the minor version (3.11) due to compatibility constraints with the scientific stack and AmberTools integration.

## Dependency Management

### Core Dependencies

The package declares core dependencies with specific version pins to maintain stability:

```mermaid
graph LR
    GMX["gmx_MMPBSA"]
    
    subgraph "Scientific Computing"
        NUMPY["numpy==1.26.4<br/>Array operations"]
        SCIPY["scipy==1.14.1<br/>Scientific computing"]
        PANDAS["pandas==1.5.3<br/>Data structures"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Visualization"
        MPT["matplotlib==3.7.3<br/>Plotting"]
        SEABORN["seaborn==0.11.2<br/>Statistical plots"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Parallel & Topology"
        MPI["mpi4py==4.0.1<br/>MPI bindings"]
        PARMED["parmed>=4.2.2<br/>Topology conversion"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Utilities"
        TQDM["tqdm<br/>Progress bars"]
    end
    
    GMX --> NUMPY
    GMX --> SCIPY
    GMX --> PANDAS
    GMX --> MPT
    GMX --> SEABORN
    GMX --> MPI
    GMX --> PARMED
    GMX --> TQDM
```

Sources: [setup.py:50-55]()

**Version Pinning Strategy:**

- **Exact pins** (`==`): Used for `numpy`, `pandas`, `matplotlib`, `scipy`, `seaborn`, and `mpi4py` to ensure consistent numerical results and avoid API breakage.
- **Minimum version** (`>=`): Used for `parmed` to allow bug fixes while maintaining compatibility with topology conversion logic.
- **No pin**: Used for `tqdm` which has a stable API.

The [setup.py:50-55]() `install_requires` list specifies these dependencies.

### Optional Dependencies

PyQt (PyQt5 or PyQt6) is an optional dependency required only for the analyzer GUI (`gmx_MMPBSA_ana`). The application logic in `app.py` dynamically checks for these modules:

```python
# From GMXMMPBSA/app.py
try:
    from PyQt6.QtWidgets import QApplication
    pyqt = True
except:
    try:
        from PyQt5.QtWidgets import QApplication
        pyqt = True
    except:
        pyqt = False
```

Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/app.py:124-132]()

If neither is found, the analyzer is disabled with a `GMXMMPBSA_ERROR` [GMXMMPBSA/app.py:134-136](). This separation allows headless installations on compute nodes.

## Version Management with Versioneer

gmx_MMPBSA uses [versioneer](https://github.com/python-versioneer/python-versioneer) for automatic version string generation from Git repository state.

```mermaid
graph LR
    GIT["Git Repository<br/>tags and commits"]
    VERSIONEER_PY["versioneer.py<br/>Version extraction"]
    VERSION_PY["GMXMMPBSA/_version.py<br/>Generated module"]
    SETUP_GET["setup.py<br/>get_version()"]
    INIT_PY["GMXMMPBSA/__init__.py<br/>__version__"]
    
    GIT --> VERSIONEER_PY
    VERSIONEER_PY --> VERSION_PY
    VERSION_PY --> SETUP_GET
    VERSION_PY --> INIT_PY
```

Sources: [setup.py:20](), [setup.py:31-32](), [GMXMMPBSA/__init__.py:34-35]()

**Versioneer Integration:**

1. [setup.py:20]() imports `versioneer`.
2. [setup.py:31]() retrieves the version: `version=versioneer.get_version()`.
3. [GMXMMPBSA/__init__.py:34-35]() imports the generated version: `from . import _version; __version__ = _version.get_versions()['version']`.
4. [setup.cfg:1-7]() provides the configuration for `versioneer`, specifying the VCS as `git` and the style as `pep440`.

## Console Scripts Registration

The package registers four command-line applications as console scripts entry points in [setup.py:56-61]():

| Command | Module Path | Purpose |
|---------|-------------|---------|
| `gmx_MMPBSA` | `GMXMMPBSA.app:gmxmmpbsa` | Core calculation application (GROMACS engine) |
| `amber_MMPBSA` | `GMXMMPBSA.app:gmxmmpbsa_amber` | Core calculation application (AMBER engine) |
| `gmx_MMPBSA_ana` | `GMXMMPBSA.app:gmxmmpbsa_ana` | Graphical analyzer |
| `gmx_MMPBSA_test` | `GMXMMPBSA.app:gmxmmpbsa_test` | Installation validator |

The `app.py` module acts as the router for these commands. For example, `gmxmmpbsa()` and `gmxmmpbsa_amber()` both call the internal `_gmxmmpbsa_base` function with different engine parameters [GMXMMPBSA/app.py:116-121]().

## Package Data Inclusion

Non-Python resources are included in the distribution through the `package_data` directive in [setup.py:34]():

- **`data/*`**: General data files.
- **`data/gmxMMPBSA/*`**: MMPBSA-specific configuration and reference files.
- **`data/xvv_files/*`**: 3D-RISM susceptibility files.
- **`analyzer/style/*`**: Qt stylesheet files for GUI theming.
- **`GMXMMPBSA.sh`**: Bash completion script.

The inclusion of these files is also supported by [MANIFEST.in:1-3](), which ensures `versioneer.py` and `_version.py` are included in source distributions.

## Distribution and CI/CD

The repository utilizes GitHub Actions for automated documentation deployment and package publishing.

### Documentation Deployment
The workflow defined in [.github/workflows/gh-pages.yml:1-36]() automates documentation updates. It:
1. Installs documentation dependencies from [docs/requirements.txt:1-6]().
2. Uses `mike` to deploy documentation versions [ .github/workflows/gh-pages.yml:34-35]().
3. Supports version-specific documentation through release tags [.github/workflows/gh-pages_tags.yml:1-38]().

### Package Publishing
The workflow in [.github/workflows/python-publish.yml:1-50]() handles PyPI distribution when a release is created:
1. Checks out the release tag [.github/workflows/python-publish.yml:15-20]().
2. Builds the package using the `build` module [.github/workflows/python-publish.yml:42]().
3. Publishes the resulting `dist/*` files to PyPI using `twine` [.github/workflows/python-publish.yml:50]().

### Conda and Pip Installation
For reproducible setups, the project provides a shell script [scripts/conda_pip_install.sh:1-32]() that demonstrates the recommended installation flow:
1. Create a Conda environment with Python 3.11 [scripts/conda_pip_install.sh:9]().
2. Install non-pip packages (`ambertools`, `gromacs`) via Conda [scripts/conda_pip_install.sh:17-18]().
3. Install scientific dependencies and `gmx_MMPBSA` via Pip [scripts/conda_pip_install.sh:21-28]().
4. Validate the installation using `gmx_MMPBSA_test` [scripts/conda_pip_install.sh:31]().

Sources: [setup.py:19-62](), [GMXMMPBSA/app.py:1-169](), [.github/workflows/python-publish.yml:1-50](), [scripts/conda_pip_install.sh:1-32]()

# Page: Documentation System

# Documentation System

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

- [mkdocs.yml](mkdocs.yml)
- [notebooks/gmx_MMPBSA_Colab.ipynb](notebooks/gmx_MMPBSA_Colab.ipynb)
