This page documents the static documentation system used to generate the gmx_MMPBSA documentation website. The system is built on MkDocs Material with multi-version support via Mike and automated deployment through GitHub Actions.

## System Overview

The gmx_MMPBSA documentation uses a static site generation approach based on **MkDocs Material 8.1.6**, providing a searchable, versioned documentation website. The system transforms Markdown files in the `docs/` directory into a deployable HTML site with navigation, search, syntax highlighting, and custom styling.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Source Files"
        MKDOCS_YML["mkdocs.yml<br/>Main Configuration"]
        DOCS_MD["docs/*.md<br/>Content Pages"]
        EXAMPLES["docs/examples/<br/>Tutorial Pages"]
        OVERRIDES["docs/overrides/<br/>Custom Templates"]
        ASSETS["docs/assets/<br/>CSS/JS/Images"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Build System"
        MKDOCS["mkdocs CLI<br/>Site Builder"]
        MATERIAL["mkdocs-material 8.1.6<br/>Theme Engine"]
        PLUGINS["Plugin Pipeline<br/>search, minify, git-date"]
        EXTENSIONS["Markdown Extensions<br/>pymdownx suite"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Version Management"
        MIKE["mike 1.1.2<br/>Version Manager"]
        GIT_VERSIONS["Git Branches/Tags<br/>Source Versions"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output"
        SITE["site/ Directory<br/>Static HTML/CSS/JS"]
        DEPLOY["GitHub Pages<br/>Deployed Site"]
    end
    
    MKDOCS_YML --> MKDOCS
    DOCS_MD --> MKDOCS
    EXAMPLES --> MKDOCS
    OVERRIDES --> MATERIAL
    ASSETS --> SITE
    
    MKDOCS --> MATERIAL
    MATERIAL --> PLUGINS
    PLUGINS --> EXTENSIONS
    EXTENSIONS --> SITE
    
    GIT_VERSIONS --> MIKE
    MIKE --> SITE
    SITE --> DEPLOY
```

**Sources:** [mkdocs.yml:1-231](), [docs/requirements.txt:1-7]()

## Core Configuration

The documentation system is configured through `mkdocs.yml`, which defines site metadata, theme settings, navigation structure, and plugin behavior.

### Site Metadata and Repository

```yaml
site_name: gmx_MMPBSA Documentation
site_url: https://valdes-tresanco-ms.github.io/gmx_MMPBSA/dev/
repo_name: gmx_MMPBSA
repo_url: https://github.com/Valdes-Tresanco-MS/gmx_MMPBSA
```

The `site_url` includes `/dev/` as the base path, indicating that Mike manages multiple versions at different URL paths [mkdocs.yml:4-4](). The `edit_uri` is set to an empty string to disable the "Edit on GitHub" links [mkdocs.yml:13-13]().

**Sources:** [mkdocs.yml:3-13]()

### Theme Configuration

The Material theme is customized with specific features and styling:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Theme: material"
        LOGO["logo: logo_white_border.svg"]
        CUSTOM["custom_dir: docs/overrides"]
        PALETTE["Dual Palette<br/>Light/Dark Mode"]
        FEATURES["Navigation Features<br/>tabs, toc.integrate, etc"]
        FONTS["Roboto/Roboto Mono"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Custom Override Files"
        MAIN_HTML["main.html<br/>Base Template Extension"]
        GLOBAL_CSS["global.css<br/>Custom Styles"]
        NEWS_JS["news.js<br/>Announcement Banner"]
    end
    
    CUSTOM --> MAIN_HTML
    CUSTOM --> GLOBAL_CSS
    CUSTOM --> NEWS_JS
```

Key theme features enabled in [mkdocs.yml:35-52]():

| Feature | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `content.code.annotate` | Inline code annotations |
| `content.tabs.link` | Synchronized content tabs |
| `navigation.expand` | Expanded sidebar by default |
| `navigation.sections` | Section grouping in sidebar |
| `navigation.tabs` | Top-level navigation tabs |
| `navigation.top` | Back-to-top button |
| `search.highlight` | Highlight search terms in results |
| `search.suggest` | Search suggestions |
| `toc.integrate` | Integrate TOC into sidebar |

The dual palette configuration allows users to toggle between light and dark modes, with color schemes defined as `primary: black` and `accent: black` for both modes [mkdocs.yml:53-78]().

**Sources:** [mkdocs.yml:19-85](), [docs/overrides/main.html:1-29]()

## Plugin System

The documentation uses three core plugins that extend MkDocs functionality:

```mermaid
graph TB
    INPUT["Markdown Input Files"]
    
    subgraph "Plugin Pipeline Order: 1→2→3"
        SEARCH["search<br/>Index Generation"]
        GIT_DATE["git-revision-date-localized<br/>Document Timestamps"]
        MINIFY["minify<br/>HTML Compression"]
    end
    
    OUTPUT["Final HTML Output"]
    
    INPUT --> SEARCH
    SEARCH --> GIT_DATE
    GIT_DATE --> MINIFY
    MINIFY --> OUTPUT
```

### Plugin Details

1. **search** - Default MkDocs search plugin that creates a search index from all documentation pages [mkdocs.yml:88-88](). Configured with `search_index_only: true` to prevent separate search page generation [mkdocs.yml:31-31]().

2. **git-revision-date-localized** - Adds creation and modification timestamps to each page footer based on git history [mkdocs.yml:89-91]():
   ```yaml
   - git-revision-date-localized:
       type: datetime
       enable_creation_date: true
   ```

3. **minify** - Compresses HTML output to reduce file sizes [mkdocs.yml:92-94]():
   ```yaml
   - minify:
       minify_html: true
   ```

**Sources:** [mkdocs.yml:87-94](), [docs/requirements.txt:1-5]()

## Markdown Extensions

The documentation system uses multiple markdown extensions, enabling advanced formatting capabilities:

### Code and Syntax Extensions

| Extension | Capability |
|-----------|-----------|
| `pymdownx.highlight` | Syntax highlighting with `anchor_linenums: true` [mkdocs.yml:127-128]() |
| `pymdownx.inlinehilite` | Inline code highlighting [mkdocs.yml:129-129]() |
| `pymdownx.superfences` | Code blocks with custom fences (including mermaid) [mkdocs.yml:137-141]() |

### Content Formatting Extensions

| Extension | Capability |
|-----------|-----------|
| `admonition` | Callout boxes (!!! syntax) [mkdocs.yml:108-108]() |
| `pymdownx.details` | Collapsible details blocks [mkdocs.yml:123-123]() |
| `pymdownx.tabbed` | Tabbed content blocks [mkdocs.yml:142-143]() |
| `pymdownx.arithmatex` | LaTeX math rendering [mkdocs.yml:117-118]() |
| `pymdownx.emoji` | Twemoji and SVG emoji support [mkdocs.yml:124-126]() |

### Special Features

The `pymdownx.superfences` extension includes custom fence configuration for mermaid diagrams [mkdocs.yml:138-141]():

```yaml
custom_fences:
  - name: mermaid
    class: mermaid
    format: !!python/name:pymdownx.superfences.fence_code_format
```

**Sources:** [mkdocs.yml:107-147]()

## Version Management with Mike

Mike provides multi-version documentation deployment, allowing users to browse documentation for different releases.

### Deployment Automation

The system uses GitHub Actions to automate documentation deployment. There are two primary workflows:

1. **Master Branch Workflow (`gh-pages.yml`)**: Triggered on pushes to the master branch. It deploys to the `dev` version and sets it as default [ .github/workflows/gh-pages.yml:1-36]().
2. **Release Workflow (`gh-pages_tags.yml`)**: Triggered when a new release is published. It extracts the tag name and deploys it as a new version using Mike [ .github/workflows/gh-pages_tags.yml:1-38]().

### Workflow Implementation

The `updatedoc` job in the master workflow performs the following steps:
- Checks out the repository with `fetch-depth: 0` (required for `git-revision-date-localized`) [ .github/workflows/gh-pages.yml:13-18]().
- Installs dependencies from `docs/requirements.txt` [ .github/workflows/gh-pages.yml:23-25]().
- Executes `mike deploy --push --rebase --update-aliases dev latest` [ .github/workflows/gh-pages.yml:34-34]().

**Sources:** [mkdocs.yml:103-104](), [docs/requirements.txt:5](), [ .github/workflows/gh-pages.yml:1-36](), [ .github/workflows/gh-pages_tags.yml:1-38]()

## Custom Assets and Styling

The documentation includes custom CSS, JavaScript, and images to enhance the default Material theme.

### Override System

The `docs/overrides/main.html` extends the base Material template to add custom blocks:

1. **Outdated version warning** - Displays a banner when viewing a non-latest version [docs/overrides/main.html:6-11]().
2. **News announcement banner** - Marquee-style news ticker loaded from `news.json` via `loadNews` function [docs/overrides/main.html:18-28]().

### Custom CSS Features

The `global.css` file provides specialized styling for parameter requirements [docs/overrides/stylesheets/global.css:35-45]():

| CSS Class | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| `.req` | Red styling for required parameters |
| `.req_optrec` | Teal styling for recommended parameters |
| `.req_opt` | Blue styling for optional parameters |

The `news.js` script dynamically calculates the marquee translation and animation duration based on content width [docs/assets/js/news.js:23-37]().

**Sources:** [docs/overrides/main.html:1-29](), [docs/overrides/stylesheets/global.css:1-145](), [docs/assets/js/news.js:1-40]()

## Contributing to Docs

Documentation is written in Markdown and stored in the `docs/` folder.

### Adding Examples

Examples are categorized by system type, analysis type, and force field support in `mkdocs.yml` [mkdocs.yml:171-224](). When adding a new example:
1. Create the appropriate directory in `docs/examples/`.
2. Add a `README.md` file.
3. Update the `nav` section in `mkdocs.yml`.

### Interactive Documentation

The documentation links to Jupyter notebooks for interactive learning:
- **Google Colab notebook**: Installs a conda environment and runs bundled examples [docs/examples/README.md:16-18]().
- **Local notebook**: For extracting data with the Python API and plotting [docs/examples/README.md:19-21]().

**Sources:** [mkdocs.yml:149-224](), [docs/examples/README.md:1-100](), [notebooks/gmx_MMPBSA_Colab.ipynb:11-26]()

# Page: Testing Infrastructure

# Testing Infrastructure

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/documentation.yml](.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/documentation.yml)

## Purpose and Scope

This document describes the testing infrastructure for gmx_MMPBSA, specifically the `gmx_MMPBSA_test` utility that validates installation and functionality. This testing system allows users to run predefined examples covering various molecular systems and analysis methods. For information about using the test utility as an end user, see [Validation with gmx_MMPBSA_test](#2.2). For information about the example files themselves, see [Example Use Cases](#6).

The testing infrastructure serves two primary purposes:
1. **Installation validation**: Verify that gmx_MMPBSA and its dependencies are correctly installed.
2. **Example demonstration**: Provide working examples of different calculation types that users can reference.

## Architecture Overview

The testing system is built around the `run_test` function, which manages the lifecycle of a test run: from cloning the necessary data to executing the calculations and launching the analyzer.

### Test Infrastructure Data Flow

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Entry Point"
        APP["gmxmmpbsa_test()<br/>app.py"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Command-Line Parsing"
        TESTPARSER["GMXMMPBSA_ArgParser<br/>commandlineparser.py"]
        PARSER_RESULT["Parsed Arguments:<br/>test, folder, reuse, nogui,<br/>num_processors, num_concurrent"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Test Execution Core"
        RUN_TEST["run_test(parser)<br/>tester.py"]
        TEST_SYS["test_sys dict<br/>Maps IDs to example paths"]
        KEY_LIST["key_list<br/>Selected test IDs"]
        TASKS["TASKS list<br/>Test commands to execute"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Parallel Runners"
        POOL["multiprocessing.Pool(num_concurrent)<br/>tester.py"]
        CALCULATESTAR["calculatestar(args)<br/>tester.py"]
        RUN_PROCESS["run_process(system, sys_name, args)<br/>tester.py"]
    end
    
    subgraph "External Tools"
        GIT["Git<br/>Clone repository"]
        GMX_MMPBSA["gmx_MMPBSA<br/>Execute via mpirun"]
        GMX_MMPBSA_ANA["gmx_MMPBSA_ana<br/>Visualize results"]
    end
    
    APP --> TESTPARSER
    TESTPARSER --> PARSER_RESULT
    PARSER_RESULT --> RUN_TEST
    
    RUN_TEST --> GIT
    RUN_TEST --> TEST_SYS
    TEST_SYS --> KEY_LIST
    
    KEY_LIST --> TASKS
    TASKS --> POOL
    POOL --> CALCULATESTAR
    CALCULATESTAR --> RUN_PROCESS
    
    RUN_PROCESS --> GMX_MMPBSA
    RUN_TEST --> GMX_MMPBSA_ANA
```

**Sources**: [GMXMMPBSA/tester.py:80-183](), [GMXMMPBSA/commandlineparser.py:189-204]()

## Command-Line Interface

The `gmx_MMPBSA_test` CLI is defined via a custom `ArgumentParser` that handles test selection, folder management, and parallel execution parameters.

| Argument | Type | Default | Description |
|----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `-t`, `--test` | `int` list | `[2]` | Test IDs to run. Supports predefined sets (0, 1, 2). |
| `-f`, `--folder` | `Path` | `.` | Directory to store cloned repository and test data. |
| `-r`, `--reuse` | flag | `False` | Reuse existing test folder instead of cloning fresh. |
| `-ng`, `--nogui` | flag | `False` | Skip opening `gmx_MMPBSA_ana` after tests complete. |
| `-n`, `--num_processors` | `int` | `1` | Number of MPI processors per calculation. |
| `-j`, `--num_concurrent` | `int` | `1` | Number of examples to run concurrently. |

**Sources**: [GMXMMPBSA/commandlineparser.py:259-313](), [GMXMMPBSA/tester.py:136-155]()

## Test Categories and Organization

The testing system organizes tests into tiers and individual test cases mapping to the `examples/` directory of the repository.

### Test Tiers

The system defines three logical sets for convenience:
* **0 (All)**: Runs all 23+ examples. [GMXMMPBSA/tester.py:136-137]()
* **1 (Minimal)**: 12 systems. Excludes slow/redundant tests like 3D-RISM or NMODE. [GMXMMPBSA/tester.py:138-140]()
* **2 (Fast)**: 9 systems. Only the shortest calculations for quick verification. [GMXMMPBSA/tester.py:141-142]()

### Individual Test Systems

The `test_sys` dictionary maps test IDs to their corresponding example paths and descriptions:

| ID | System / Method | Path |
|----|-----------------|------|
| 3 | Protein-Ligand (ST) | `Protein_ligand/ST` |
| 4 | Protein-Protein | `Protein_protein` |
| 6 | Protein-Membrane | `Protein_membrane` |
| 12| Alanine Scanning | `Alanine_scanning` |
| 14| Decomposition | `Decomposition_analysis` |
| 17| Normal Mode (NMODE) | `Entropy_calculations/nmode` |
| 18| 3D-RISM | `3D-RISM` |
| 23| QM/MMGBSA | `QM_MMGBSA` |
| 24| GBNSR6 | `GBNSR6` |

**Sources**: [GMXMMPBSA/tester.py:109-134]()

## Test Execution Workflow

### 1. Environment Preparation
The system first verifies that `git` is available. It then checks if the destination folder exists and either clones the `gmx_MMPBSA` repository (using `--depth 1` for speed) or reuses an existing one if the `-r` flag is provided. [GMXMMPBSA/tester.py:81-106]()

### 2. Task Construction
For each selected test, the system:
1. Determines the number of frames in the input file using `_get_frames`. [GMXMMPBSA/tester.py:58-71]()
2. Parses the `README.md` file in the example folder to extract the specific `gmx_MMPBSA` command. [GMXMMPBSA/tester.py:157-164]()
3. Prepends `mpirun` with the appropriate number of processors. [GMXMMPBSA/tester.py:165-171]()

### 3. Parallel Execution
The system uses `multiprocessing.Pool` to manage concurrent test execution. The `-j` flag controls how many examples run at once, while each example uses `-n` MPI ranks. [GMXMMPBSA/tester.py:175-188]()

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Process Management"
        POOL["multiprocessing.Pool<br/>(num_concurrent)"]
        IMAP["imap_unordered"]
    end

    subgraph "Individual Task"
        PROC["run_process()"]
        CHDIR["os.chdir(example_dir)"]
        LOG["Open sys_name.log"]
        SUBP["subprocess.Popen(mpirun...)"]
    end

    POOL --> IMAP
    IMAP --> PROC
    PROC --> CHDIR
    CHDIR --> LOG
    LOG --> SUBP
```

**Sources**: [GMXMMPBSA/tester.py:36-44](), [GMXMMPBSA/tester.py:175-180]()

## Implementation Details

### Frame Counting and CPU Allocation
The function `_get_frames` parses the `mmpbsa.in` file to calculate the number of snapshots. This is used to ensure the number of MPI processors does not exceed the number of frames, which would be inefficient. [GMXMMPBSA/tester.py:58-71]()

### Error Detection
The system includes specialized error detection, such as `_has_known_rism_fortran_runtime_error`, which scans log files for specific Fortran runtime issues common in RISM calculations. [GMXMMPBSA/tester.py:47-55]()

### Result Accumulation
Successful tests are added to a `result_list`. If the `-ng` (no GUI) flag is not set, the system launches `gmx_MMPBSA_ana` with all successful result folders loaded simultaneously for comparison. [GMXMMPBSA/tester.py:192-202]()

## Adding New Tests

To add a new test case to the infrastructure:

1. **Add Example**: Place the example files in the `examples/` directory of the repository.
2. **Define Test ID**: Add a new entry to the `test_sys` dictionary in `tester.py` mapping a new ID to the directory path and a description. [GMXMMPBSA/tester.py:109-134]()
3. **Update Parser**: Update the `choices` and `help` text for the `-t` argument in `commandlineparser.py` to include the new ID. [GMXMMPBSA/commandlineparser.py:269-304]()
4. **Update Tiers**: If applicable, add the ID to the `key_list` for predefined sets (0, 1, or 2). [GMXMMPBSA/tester.py:136-143]()

**Sources**: [GMXMMPBSA/tester.py:109-143](), [GMXMMPBSA/commandlineparser.py:269-304]()

---

# Troubleshooting and FAQ

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

This page provides guidance on diagnosing and resolving common issues encountered when using gmx_MMPBSA. It covers general troubleshooting strategies, the error handling system, and frequently asked questions. For category-specific issues, see the subsections: [Installation Issues](#9.1), [Calculation Errors](#9.2), and [Performance and Resource Issues](#9.3).

## Purpose and Scope

This section serves as the central resource for resolving problems with gmx_MMPBSA. It documents:

- The error handling architecture and exception hierarchy.
- Common diagnostic workflows and commands.
- Where to find help beyond this documentation.
- General troubleshooting strategies applicable across all issue types.

For detailed solutions to specific problem categories, refer to the subsections. For examples of correct usage, see [Example Use Cases](#6).

## Help Resources

gmx_MMPBSA provides multiple channels for troubleshooting assistance:

| Resource | Purpose | Location |
|----------|---------|----------|
| **Documentation** | Comprehensive guides and examples | [Online Docs](https://valdes-tresanco-ms.github.io/gmx_MMPBSA/dev/getting-started/) |
| **Google Group** | Community discussion forum | [gmx_mmpbsa group](https://groups.google.com/g/gmx_mmpbsa) |
| **Issue Tracker** | Bug reports and feature requests | [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/Valdes-Tresanco-MS/gmx_MMPBSA/issues) |
| **Q&A Section** | Frequently asked questions | [docs/Q&A/README.md:1-19]() |

Before opening a new issue, search existing issues and Google Group posts for similar problems. The log file `gmx_MMPBSA.log` is essential for diagnosis—always include relevant excerpts when seeking help.

**Sources:** [docs/Q&A/README.md:1-19]()

## Exception Hierarchy and Error System

gmx_MMPBSA implements a hierarchical exception system for structured error handling. All exceptions inherit from the `MMPBSA_Error` base class.

### Exception Class Hierarchy

```mermaid
graph TB
    BASE["MMPBSA_Error<br/>(Base Exception)"]
    WRAPPER["GMXMMPBSA_ERROR<br/>(Logging Wrapper)"]
    
    BASE --> TimerException["TimerException<br/>Timer module errors"]
    BASE --> CommandlineError["CommandlineError<br/>CLI parsing errors"]
    BASE --> CalcError["CalcError<br/>Calculation failures"]
    BASE --> SetupError["SetupError<br/>Environment setup"]
    BASE --> PrmtopError["PrmtopError<br/>Topology file errors"]
    BASE --> SelectionError["SelectionError<br/>Invalid residue selection"]
    BASE --> TrajError["TrajError<br/>Trajectory processing"]
    BASE --> InputError["InputError<br/>Input file errors"]
    BASE --> IllegalOption["IllegalOption<br/>Incompatible options"]
    BASE --> InterruptError["InterruptError<br/>Process interruption"]
    BASE --> OutputError["OutputError<br/>Output parsing errors"]
    
    BASE --> InconsistentError1["InconsistentError1<br/>BOND/ANGLE/DIHED<br/>inconsistency"]
    BASE --> InconsistentError2["InconsistentError2<br/>1-4 VDW/EEL<br/>inconsistency"]
    BASE --> ConvergenceError["ConvergenceError<br/>NMODE minimization"]
    
    BASE --> MutateError["MutateError<br/>Alanine scanning"]
    MutateError --> MutantResError["MutantResError<br/>Invalid mutation target"]
    
    BASE --> CreateInputError["CreateInputError<br/>MDIN file generation"]
    BASE --> LengthError["LengthError<br/>EnergyVector mismatch"]
    BASE --> DecompError["DecompError<br/>Decomposition parsing"]
    BASE --> InternalError["InternalError<br/>Programming errors"]
    BASE --> NoFileExists["NoFileExists<br/>Missing required files"]
    
    WRAPPER -.wraps.-> BASE
    
    WARN["MMPBSA_Warning<br/>(Base Warning)"]
    WARN --> InputWarning["InputWarning<br/>Non-fatal warnings"]
    WARN --> StabilityWarning["StabilityWarning<br/>Stability calc warnings"]
```

The error system is designed to provide specific feedback for different failure modes, such as `CalcError` for calculation failures and `TrajError` for trajectory processing issues.

**Sources:** [docs/Q&A/calculations.md:15-16](), [docs/Q&A/installation.md:40]()

## Diagnostic Workflow

When encountering issues, follow this systematic troubleshooting approach:

```mermaid
graph TB
    START["Issue Encountered"]
    
    START --> CHECK_LOG["Check gmx_MMPBSA.log"]
    CHECK_LOG --> IDENTIFY["Identify Exception Type"]
    
    IDENTIFY --> INSTALL_Q{"Installation<br/>Related?"}
    IDENTIFY --> CALC_Q{"Calculation<br/>Related?"}
    IDENTIFY --> OS_Q{"OS/GUI<br/>Related?"}
    
    INSTALL_Q -->|Yes| INSTALL_SEC["See Section 9.1<br/>Installation Issues"]
    CALC_Q -->|Yes| CALC_SEC["See Section 9.2<br/>Calculation Errors"]
    OS_Q -->|Yes| OS_SEC["Check OS Compatibility"]
    
    INSTALL_SEC --> CHECK_ENV["Verify Dependencies<br/>Check PATH<br/>Test with gmx_MMPBSA_test"]
    CALC_SEC --> CHECK_INPUT["Validate Input Files<br/>Check Structure Consistency<br/>Review Input Parameters"]
    OS_SEC --> CHECK_GUI["Verify Qt Libraries<br/>Check nogui option<br/>Check OS version"]
    
    CHECK_ENV --> RESOLVED_Q{"Issue<br/>Resolved?"}
    CHECK_INPUT --> RESOLVED_Q
    CHECK_GUI --> RESOLVED_Q
    
    RESOLVED_Q -->|Yes| END["Continue Work"]
    RESOLVED_Q -->|No| SEARCH["Search Google Group<br/>& GitHub Issues"]
    
    SEARCH --> FOUND_Q{"Solution<br/>Found?"}
    FOUND_Q -->|Yes| END
    FOUND_Q -->|No| REPORT["Open GitHub Issue<br/>or Google Group Post<br/>(Include log excerpt)"]
    REPORT --> END
```

**Sources:** [docs/Q&A/README.md:15-17](), [docs/Q&A/OS_issues.md:1-33]()

## Pre-Execution Validation

Before running `gmx_MMPBSA`, validate input files to prevent common errors.

### Structure and Trajectory Consistency

Input structures must be centered and properly wrapped. Broken structures cause inconsistent results and "could not convert string to float" errors in `sander`.

| Issue | Solution | Command Example |
|-------|----------|-----------------|
| **Broken Structure** | Generate from TPR | `gmx editconf -f md.tpr -o md.pdb` |
| **PBC in Trajectory** | Remove PBC | `gmx trjconv -s md.tpr -f md.xtc -o md_noPBC.xtc -pbc mol -center` |
| **Fitted Trajectory** | Remove rotation | `gmx trjconv -s md.tpr -f md_noPBC.xtc -o md_fit.xtc -fit rot+trans` |

**Sources:** [docs/Q&A/calculations.md:15-71]()

### OS and Environment Compatibility

- **macOS:** Versions lower than BigSur are generally not supported [docs/Q&A/OS_issues.md:10-14]().
- **WSL/HPC:** The analyzer (`gmx_MMPBSA_ana`) requires graphics drivers. Use the `-nogui` option on HPC systems to avoid crashes [docs/Q&A/OS_issues.md:19-33]().
- **Qt Plugins:** Errors related to `xcb` can often be fixed by reinstalling `libxcb-xinerama0` [docs/Q&A/OS_issues.md:35-45]().

## Common Diagnostic Commands

These commands help diagnose different aspects of functionality:

| Category | Command | Purpose |
|----------|---------|---------|
| **Setup** | `source amber.sh` | Ensure AmberTools environment is loaded [docs/Q&A/installation.md:14]() |
| **Setup** | `conda list gmx-mmpbsa` | Verify installation in current conda environment |
| **Calculation** | `gmx_MMPBSA --rewrite-output` | Update output files after modifying `_GMXMMPBSA_info` [docs/Q&A/calculations.md:131]() |
| **Validation** | `gmx_MMPBSA_test -t 2` | Run predefined test examples |

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Installation

**Q: I can't find the `amber.python` executable.**  
A: Ensure `AmberTools` is installed and the `amber.sh` (or `amber.csh`) file has been sourced. If using conda, the python in the conda environment should be used [docs/Q&A/installation.md:10-16]().

**Q: I get a `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'parmed'`.**  
A: This usually indicates a broken installation or an environment mismatch. Refer to GitHub issue #2 for resolution [docs/Q&A/installation.md:40-44]().

### Calculations

**Q: Why do I get very high solvation energy values with the PB model?**  
A: By default, `inp=2` includes a dispersion term that can sometimes produce unrealistic values due to error cancellation imbalances. Try setting `inp=1` in the `&pb` namelist to use a single term SASA-based model [docs/Q&A/calculations.md:103-125]().

**Q: What does `ValueError: could not convert string to float: '*************'` mean?**  
A: This usually occurs when energy values exceed 7 digits, often due to inconsistent input structures (PBC issues) or trying to calculate a group that is too large for `sander`'s output format [docs/Q&A/calculations.md:15-93]().

### Performance and Resources

For detailed information on handling memory issues, MPI configuration, and optimizing large calculations, see [Performance and Resource Issues](#9.3).

**Sources:** [docs/Q&A/calculations.md:1-148](), [docs/Q&A/installation.md:1-53](), [docs/Q&A/OS_issues.md:1-48]()

This page documents common installation problems encountered when setting up `gmx_MMPBSA` and their resolutions. It covers dependency conflicts, environment configuration issues, and platform-specific problems.

For general installation instructions, see [Installation and Setup](#2). For validation procedures after installation, see [Validation with gmx_MMPBSA_test](#2.2). For runtime calculation errors, see [Calculation Errors](#9.2).

## Python Version Enforcement

`gmx_MMPBSA` enforces a strict Python version requirement that is a common source of installation failures.

### The Python 3.11 Requirement

The `setup.py` file contains a hard version check that prevents installation with any Python version other than 3.11:

```python
if sys.version_info[:2] != (3, 11):
    raise RuntimeError("gmx_MMPBSA requires python == 3.11")
```

**Sources:** [setup.py:26-27]()

This check executes immediately when `pip install` attempts to install the package, causing the installation to abort with:

```
RuntimeError: gmx_MMPBSA requires python == 3.11
```

### Resolution Strategy

| Installation Method | Solution |
|-------------------|----------|
| Conda environment | Use `python=3.11` in environment creation: `conda create -n gmxMMPBSA python=3.11` |
| AmberTools compilation | Ensure AmberTools' bundled Python is version 3.11 before installation |
| Existing environment | Create a new Python 3.11 environment; in-place upgrades/downgrades are not supported |

**Sources:** [setup.py:26-27](), [docs/installation.md:79-80](), [docs/env.yml:6]()

### Installation Method Decision Tree

```mermaid
graph TB
    START["User wants to install gmx_MMPBSA"]
    CHECK_PYTHON{"Python 3.11<br/>available?"}
    METHOD{"Installation<br/>preference?"}
    
    CONDA_PATH["Conda Environment Method"]
    AMBER_PATH["AmberTools Compilation Method"]
    
    CONDA_YML["Use env.yml"]
    CONDA_MANUAL["Manual conda setup"]
    
    AMBER_CHECK{"AmberTools<br/>compiled?"}
    AMBER_COMPILE["Compile AmberTools 20/21/22/23"]
    AMBER_INSTALL["amber.python -m pip install gmx_MMPBSA"]
    
    PIP_INSTALL["python -m pip install gmx_MMPBSA"]
    
    VALIDATE["Run gmx_MMPBSA_test"]
    
    START --> CHECK_PYTHON
    CHECK_PYTHON -->|No| METHOD
    CHECK_PYTHON -->|Yes| METHOD
    
    METHOD -->|Recommended| CONDA_PATH
    METHOD -->|Advanced| AMBER_PATH
    
    CONDA_PATH --> CONDA_YML
    CONDA_PATH --> CONDA_MANUAL
    
    CONDA_YML --> PIP_INSTALL
    CONDA_MANUAL --> PIP_INSTALL
    
    AMBER_PATH --> AMBER_CHECK
    AMBER_CHECK -->|No| AMBER_COMPILE
    AMBER_CHECK -->|Yes| AMBER_INSTALL
    AMBER_COMPILE --> AMBER_INSTALL
    
    PIP_INSTALL --> VALIDATE
    AMBER_INSTALL --> VALIDATE
```

**Sources:** [docs/installation.md:19-32](), [setup.py:26-27]()

## Dependency Conflict Patterns

### Core Scientific Stack Version Requirements

The `setup.py` and `env.yml` files specify exact versions for the scientific computing stack to ensure compatibility:

| Package | Required Version | Common Conflict Source |

| `pandas` | `1.5.3` | General data analysis environments |
| `matplotlib` | `3.7.3` | System-wide visualization tools |
| `scipy` | `1.14.1` | Scientific computing packages |
| `mpi4py` | `4.0.1` | HPC system-wide installations |
| `parmed` | `<5` (typically `4.2.2`) | Topology handling tools |
| `seaborn` | `0.11.2` | Plotting libraries |

**Sources:** [setup.py:46-51](), [docs/env.yml:20-29](), [docs/installation.md:83-86]()

## PATH and Environment Configuration Issues

### Console Script Registration Problem

After installation, users may find that `gmx_MMPBSA` is not recognized as a command. This occurs because `setup.py` registers three console scripts that pip installs to the Python environment's `bin/` directory:

```python
entry_points={
    "console_scripts": [
        "gmx_MMPBSA=GMXMMPBSA.app:gmxmmpbsa",
        "gmx_MMPBSA_ana=GMXMMPBSA.app:gmxmmpbsa_ana",
        "gmx_MMPBSA_test=GMXMMPBSA.app:gmxmmpbsa_test"]}
```

**Sources:** [setup.py:52-56](), [docs/Q&A/installation.md:32-39]()

### Resolution Options

**1. Check PATH:** Ensure the bin folder of your conda environment is in the `PATH`.
**2. Activation:** Always activate the environment before use: `conda activate gmxMMPBSA`.
**3. Permissions:** Check if the application has execution permissions.

**Sources:** [docs/Q&A/installation.md:32-39](), [GMXMMPBSA/GMXMMPBSA.sh:23-39]()

### Environment Activation State Machine

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> NotInstalled: Fresh system
    
    NotInstalled --> Installed: pip install gmx_MMPBSA
    
    Installed --> PathNotSet: Scripts not in PATH
    Installed --> PathSet: PATH configured
    
    PathNotSet --> ManualPath: export PATH=.../bin:$PATH
    PathNotSet --> CondaInit: conda activate gmxMMPBSA
    
    ManualPath --> PathSet
    
    PathSet --> Executable: gmx_MMPBSA available
    
    Executable --> [*]: Successfully running
```

**Sources:** [docs/installation.md:51-53](), [docs/Q&A/installation.md:32-39]()

## AmberTools-Related Issues

### Missing AmberTools Installation

`gmx_MMPBSA` requires **AmberTools20 or 21** (and has been tested with newer versions up to 24 in some contexts) to be installed. It depends on several executables:

- `sander` - GB/PB energy calculations.
- `rism3d.snglpnt` - 3D-RISM calculations.
- `mmpbsa_py_nabnmode` - Normal mode entropy calculations.
- `cpptraj` - Trajectory processing.

**Sources:** [docs/installation.md:8-9](), [docs/env.yml:9-21](), [docs/summary.md:18-29]()

### AmberTools Detection Issues

**Problem:** `amber.python` executable not found.
**Solution:** Ensure `AmberTools` is installed and the `amber.sh` (or `amber.csh`) file is sourced. If installed via conda, use the python executable from that environment.

**Sources:** [docs/Q&A/installation.md:10-16]()

## MPI and Parallelism Issues

### mpi4py Installation Failures

**Problem:** Error: "Cannot compile MPI programs. Check your configuration!!!"
**Solution:** Install or reinstall the OpenMPI library:
```bash
sudo apt install openmpi-bin libopenmpi-dev openssh-client
```
**Sources:** [docs/Q&A/installation.md:17-31]()

### MPI Version Requirements
The project specifies `mpi4py=4.0.1`. In HPC environments, this must be compatible with the system's MPI implementation.

**Sources:** [docs/env.yml:22](), [docs/installation.md:83]()

## OS and GUI Specific Issues

### WSL and Remote GUI
**Problem:** `gmx_MMPBSA_ana` fails in Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL).
**Cause:** WSL lacks native graphics drivers for Linux GUI applications.
**HPC Usage:** Use the `-nogui` flag to prevent the analyzer from launching automatically after calculations.

**Sources:** [docs/Q&A/OS_issues.md:16-34](), [docs/gmx_MMPBSA_command-line.md:60-61]()

### Qt Plugin Errors
**Problem:** `qt.qpa.plugin: Could not load the Qt platform plugin "xcb"`.
**Solution:** Reinstall the `libxcb-xinerama0` library:
```bash
sudo apt install --reinstall libxcb-xinerama0
```
**Sources:** [docs/Q&A/OS_issues.md:35-47]()

### macOS Compatibility
`gmx_MMPBSA` has been tested on macOS BigSur. Versions lower than BigSur are assumed to be incompatible.

**Sources:** [docs/Q&A/OS_issues.md:10-15]()

## Validation After Installation

After resolving installation issues, validate the setup using `gmx_MMPBSA_test`:

```bash
# Activate environment
conda activate gmxMMPBSA

# Run a specific test example (e.g., test 1)
gmx_MMPBSA_test -t 1
```

**Sources:** [docs/installation.md:52-53](), [GMXMMPBSA/GMXMMPBSA.sh:109](), [docs/summary.md:46-47]()

# Page: Calculation Errors

# Calculation Errors

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [GMXMMPBSA/API.py](GMXMMPBSA/API.py)
- [GMXMMPBSA/amber_outputs.py](GMXMMPBSA/amber_outputs.py)
- [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py](GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py)
- [GMXMMPBSA/output_file.py](GMXMMPBSA/output_file.py)
- [docs/Q&A/OS_issues.md](docs/Q&A/OS_issues.md)
- [docs/Q&A/calculations.md](docs/Q&A/calculations.md)
- [docs/Q&A/installation.md](docs/Q&A/installation.md)
- [docs/assets/images/q_a/inconsistent_str.png](docs/assets/images/q_a/inconsistent_str.png)
- [docs/assets/images/q_a/traj_comp.gif](docs/assets/images/q_a/traj_comp.gif)

</details>



This page documents common calculation failures, input file errors, and debugging strategies for gmx_MMPBSA.

## Overview

Calculation errors in gmx_MMPBSA can occur at multiple stages of the pipeline: during input validation, topology generation, trajectory processing, energy calculations, or output processing. The application utilizes a robust exception system and detailed logging to help users identify the root cause of failures.

## Error Classification

gmx_MMPBSA uses a hierarchical exception system defined in `GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py`. All calculation-related errors inherit from the base `MMPBSA_Error` class.

### Exception Hierarchy

```mermaid
graph TB
    BASE["MMPBSA_Error [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:25]"]
    
    INPUT["InputError [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:80]"]
    CALC["CalcError [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:55]"]
    TRAJ["TrajError [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:75]"]
    PRMTOP["PrmtopError [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:65]"]
    SELECT["SelectionError [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:70]"]
    ILLEGAL["IllegalOption [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:85]"]
    OUTPUT["OutputError [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:95]"]
    CONSIST1["InconsistentError1 [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:100]"]
    CONSIST2["InconsistentError2 [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:107]"]
    CONVERG["ConvergenceError [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:114]"]
    MUTATE["MutateError [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:119]"]
    CREATEIN["CreateInputError [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:129]"]
    DECOMP["DecompError [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:141]"]
    NOFILE["NoFileExists [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:151]"]
    
    BASE --> INPUT
    BASE --> CALC
    BASE --> TRAJ
    BASE --> PRMTOP
    BASE --> SELECT
    BASE --> ILLEGAL
    BASE --> OUTPUT
    BASE --> CONSIST1
    BASE --> CONSIST2
    BASE --> CONVERG
    BASE --> MUTATE
    BASE --> CREATEIN
    BASE --> DECOMP
    BASE --> NOFILE
    
    MUTATE --> MUTANTRES["MutantResError [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:124]"]
```

**Sources:** [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:25-153]()

## Numerical and Format Errors

### ValueError: could not convert string to float: '*************'

This is one of the most frequent errors reported. It occurs when `sander` (the underlying calculation engine from AmberTools) produces output values that exceed the allocated field width in its text-based output files.

| Cause | Code Entity Impacted | Solution |
|-------|----------------------|----------|
| **Broken Structure/PBC** | `make_trajs.py` | Ensure PBC is removed and molecules are centered using `gmx trjconv`. |
| **System Too Large** | `sander` (external) | Modify calculation parameters (e.g., `intdiel`) or use a sub-system. |
| **High Solvation Energy** | `&pb` namelist | Switch `inp=2` (default) to `inp=1` to avoid the `EDISPER` term. |

**Sources:** [docs/Q&A/calculations.md:15-101]()

### PB Solvation Energy Imbalances

When using the Poisson-Boltzmann (PB) model, unrealistic values can arise from the `EDISPER` (dispersion) contribution.

- **Symptom:** Unusually high non-polar solvation energy.
- **Mechanism:** `inp=2` models non-polar energy as cavity + dispersion. `inp=1` models it as a single term proportional to SASA.
- **Fix:** Set `inp=1` in the `&pb` namelist of `mmpbsa.in`.

**Sources:** [docs/Q&A/calculations.md:103-148]()

## Trajectory and Topology Consistency

### Inconsistent Potential Terms

The classes `InconsistentError1` and `InconsistentError2` are raised when internal potential terms (BOND, ANGLE, DIHEDRAL, 1-4 VDW, 1-4 EEL) do not match between the complex and the sum of its components (receptor + ligand).

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Calculation Orchestration [GMXMMPBSA/calculation.py]"
        CALC["CalculationList"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Data Collection [GMXMMPBSA/amber_outputs.py]"
        AO["AmberOutput Class"]
        EV["EnergyVector"]
    end
    
    CALC -->|Extracts Data| AO
    AO -->|Stores Frames| EV
    EV -->|Comparison| CHECK{Diff > 0.1?}
    CHECK -->|Yes| ERR["InconsistentError [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:100]"]
```

**Sources:** [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:100-111](), [GMXMMPBSA/amber_outputs.py:104-107]()

### Trajectory Preparation Checklist

To avoid `TrajError` or inconsistent energies, follow this `gmx trjconv` protocol:
1. **Center:** Use a group containing both receptor and ligand.
2. **PBC Removal:** Use `-pbc mol -ur compact`.
3. **Fitting:** Use `-fit rot+trans` (optional but recommended for NMODE).

**Sources:** [docs/Q&A/calculations.md:43-85]()

## Specific Calculation Failures

### NMODE Convergence Issues

`ConvergenceError` occurs when a frame fails to minimize within the specified `maxcyc` or `drms` tolerance.

- **Indicator:** `self.no_nmode_convergence` is set to `True` in `AmberOutput`.
- **Debugging:** Check `gmx_MMPBSA.log` to see which frames failed. If many frames fail, consider increasing `maxcyc` or relaxing `drms`.

**Sources:** [GMXMMPBSA/amber_outputs.py:87-87](), [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:114-116]()

### Interaction Entropy (IE) Unreliability

The Interaction Entropy method requires the standard deviation of the interaction energy ($\sigma_{IE}$) to be small.

- **Threshold:** If $\sigma_{IE} > 3.6$ kcal/mol, the results are considered unreliable.
- **Code implementation:** The `IEout` class in `amber_outputs.py` handles the parsing and statistics for these calculations.

**Sources:** [GMXMMPBSA/amber_outputs.py:40-40](), [docs/Q&A/calculations.md:149-160]()

## Output and Parsing Errors

### Output Parsing Logic

The `AmberOutput` class and its derivatives (like `IEout`, `C2out`, `NMODEout`) are responsible for reading `sander` output files.

```mermaid
graph LR
    FILE["sander.out.#"] -->|Parse| AO["AmberOutput._read()"]
    AO -->|Fill| COMP["_fill_composite_terms()"]
    COMP -->|Result| EV["EnergyVector"]
    EV -->|Write| CSV["CSV Output [GMXMMPBSA/output_file.py]"]
```

**Sources:** [GMXMMPBSA/amber_outputs.py:65-110](), [GMXMMPBSA/output_file.py:64-67]()

### Data Keys and Components

Errors in parsing often stem from unexpected components in the output. The `data_key_owner` dictionary maps energy terms to their categories (`GGAS`, `GSOLV`, `TOTAL`).

| Term | Category | Source |
|------|----------|--------|
| BOND, ANGLE, DIHED | GGAS | Gas Phase |
| EPB, ENPOLAR | GSOLV | PB Solvation |
| EGB, ESURF | GSOLV | GB Solvation |
| ESCF | GGAS | QM/GB |

**Sources:** [GMXMMPBSA/amber_outputs.py:44-62]()

## Debugging Strategies

1. **Check the Log:** `gmx_MMPBSA.log` is the primary source for identifying which specific command (e.g., `sander`, `cpptraj`, `tleap`) failed.
2. **Rewrite Output:** Use `gmx_MMPBSA --rewrite-output` to regenerate the summary file without re-running expensive calculations if you only need to change metadata or filtering.
3. **API Access:** For custom debugging, use the `MMPBSA_API` to load results into a Python environment and inspect the `EnergyVector` objects directly.

**Sources:** [GMXMMPBSA/exceptions.py:170-171](), [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:2-6](), [docs/Q&A/calculations.md:131-131]()

---

# Page: Performance and Resource Issues

# Performance and Resource Issues

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [GMXMMPBSA/fake_mpi.py](GMXMMPBSA/fake_mpi.py)
- [docs/Q&A/OS_issues.md](docs/Q&A/OS_issues.md)
- [docs/Q&A/calculations.md](docs/Q&A/calculations.md)
- [docs/Q&A/installation.md](docs/Q&A/installation.md)
- [docs/assets/images/q_a/inconsistent_str.png](docs/assets/images/q_a/inconsistent_str.png)
- [docs/assets/images/q_a/traj_comp.gif](docs/assets/images/q_a/traj_comp.gif)

</details>



This page addresses common performance bottlenecks and resource management issues in gmx_MMPBSA calculations. For installation-related problems, see [Installation Issues](#9.1). For errors during calculations, see [Calculation Errors](#9.2).

## Overview

gmx_MMPBSA calculations can be computationally demanding, involving:

- Large trajectory processing requiring significant memory
- Parallel calculations using MPI for frame distribution
- Multiple external program calls (sander, cpptraj, gbnsr6, etc.)
- Generation of temporary files and intermediate data
- Per-residue decomposition analysis generating extensive output

Performance issues typically manifest as excessive memory consumption, slow calculation times, MPI failures, or disk space exhaustion.

---

## Memory Usage Patterns

### Frame Distribution and Memory Requirements

The primary memory consumer in gmx_MMPBSA is the trajectory processing and energy calculation phase. The system distributes frames across MPI ranks to enable parallel processing.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Memory Architecture"
        INPUT["Input Trajectories<br/>complex.xtc/nc"]
        SPLIT["Frame Distribution<br/>make_trajectories()"]
        
        subgraph "MPI Rank 0"
            R0_MEM["Frames 1-N/P<br/>~X MB per frame"]
            R0_CALC["sander/cpptraj<br/>calculations"]
        end
        
        subgraph "MPI Rank 1"
            R1_MEM["Frames N/P+1-2N/P<br/>~X MB per frame"]
            R1_CALC["sander/cpptraj<br/>calculations"]
        end
        
        subgraph "MPI Rank P-1"
            RP_MEM["Frames (P-1)N/P+1-N<br/>~X MB per frame"]
            RP_CALC["sander/cpptraj<br/>calculations"]
        end
        
        MERGE["Results Collection<br/>Master rank only"]
        OUTPUT["FINAL_RESULTS_MMPBSA.dat"]
    end
    
    INPUT --> SPLIT
    SPLIT --> R0_MEM
    SPLIT --> R1_MEM
    SPLIT --> RP_MEM
    
    R0_MEM --> R0_CALC
    R1_MEM --> R1_CALC
    RP_MEM --> RP_CALC
    
    R0_CALC --> MERGE
    R1_CALC --> MERGE
    RP_CALC --> MERGE
    
    MERGE --> OUTPUT
```

**Memory Scaling Per Rank**:
- Base trajectory data: ~5-10 MB per frame (depends on system size)
- Working memory for sander: ~100-500 MB per process
- PB calculations: 2-10× more memory than GB
- NMODE calculations: Additional ~200-800 MB depending on system size

Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/make_trajs.py:84-108](), [GMXMMPBSA/main.py:218-225]()

### Memory Warnings

gmx_MMPBSA issues memory warnings for specific calculation types:

```python
# From main.py
if (self.INPUT['pb']['pbrun'] or self.INPUT['rism']['rismrun'] or
    self.INPUT['nmode']['nmoderun']) and self.mpi_size > 1:
    logging.warning('PB/RISM/NMODE will be calculated with multiple threads, make sure you have enough RAM.')
```

This warning appears because:
- **PB calculations** solve the Poisson-Boltzmann equation on a grid, requiring substantial memory.
- **RISM calculations** involve 3D grids for solvent distribution.
- **NMODE calculations** compute Hessian matrices for entropy estimation.

Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/main.py:223-225]()

### Decomposition Analysis Memory Impact

Per-residue and pairwise decomposition analysis can generate massive amounts of data:

| Decomposition Mode | Energy Terms | Molecules | Residues | Total Items | Memory Impact |
|:-------------------|:-------------|:----------|:---------|:------------|:--------------|
| `idecomp=1` | 6 | 3 | N | 18N | Moderate |
| `idecomp=2` | 6 | 3 | N | 18N | Moderate |
| `idecomp=3` | 6 | 3 | N² | 18N² | **High** |
| `idecomp=4` | 6 | 3 | N² | 18N² | **High** |

With `dec_verbose` levels (0-3), the multiplier increases from 1× to 12×. gmx_MMPBSA warns about large decomposition selections when `total_items > 250` [GMXMMPBSA/make_top.py:164-180]().

Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/make_top.py:164-180]()

---

## MPI Configuration and Parallelization

### Frame Distribution Strategy

gmx_MMPBSA uses MPI to distribute frames across processors. The distribution algorithm ensures balanced workload:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Frame Distribution Logic"
        TOTAL["Total Frames: N"]
        SIZE["MPI Size: P"]
        
        BASE["Base per rank:<br/>N // P"]
        EXTRA["Extra frames:<br/>N % P"]
        
        ASSIGN["Assignment Logic"]
        
        R0["Rank 0:<br/>base + 1 frame"]
        R1["Rank 1:<br/>base + 1 frame"]
        RX["Rank X:<br/>base frames"]
        
        TOTAL --> BASE
        TOTAL --> EXTRA
        SIZE --> BASE
        
        BASE --> ASSIGN
        EXTRA --> ASSIGN
        
        ASSIGN --> R0
        ASSIGN --> R1
        ASSIGN --> RX
    end
```

**Distribution Code**:
```python
# From make_trajs.py
frames_per_rank = traj.processed_frames // size
extras = traj.processed_frames - frames_per_rank * size
frame_count = [frames_per_rank for i in range(size)]
for i in range(size):
    if i < extras: frame_count[i] += 1
```

If the number of frames is less than the MPI size, the application will terminate with an error [GMXMMPBSA/make_trajs.py:79-88](). For serial execution where MPI is not installed, `fake_mpi.py` provides a fallback `Communicator` class that returns a rank of 0 and size of 1 [GMXMMPBSA/fake_mpi.py:28-69]().

Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/make_trajs.py:79-88](), [GMXMMPBSA/fake_mpi.py:28-69]()

### MPI-Specific Issues

**1. Thread Safety and Environment**

Each MPI rank calls external programs independently. In HPC environments, the GUI must be disabled using the `-nogui` flag to avoid errors related to graphics libraries [docs/Q&A/OS_issues.md:29-33]().

**2. File System Contention**

Multiple MPI ranks writing temporary files simultaneously can cause I/O bottlenecks. Output files are typically suffixed with the rank index (e.g., `.0`, `.1`) to prevent collisions [GMXMMPBSA/calculation.py:295-299]().

**3. Non-Uniform Calculation Times**

Some frames may take longer to calculate, particularly NMODE where convergence might fail. If convergence is not reached, terms are set to `NaN` [GMXMMPBSA/amber_outputs.py:561-566]().

Sources: [docs/Q&A/OS_issues.md:29-33](), [GMXMMPBSA/calculation.py:295-299](), [GMXMMPBSA/amber_outputs.py:561-566]()

---

## Disk Space and I/O Management

### Temporary File Generation

gmx_MMPBSA generates extensive temporary files. The `keep_files` parameter in `&general` namelist controls temporary file retention:

| Value | Behavior | Use Case |
|:------|:---------|:---------|
| `0` | Delete all temporary files | Production runs, disk space limited |
| `1` | Keep input files (`.mdin`, topology) | Debugging input generation |
| `2` | Keep all files | Full debugging, method development |

Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/main.py:398-407](), [docs/Q&A/calculations.md:127-132]()

### NetCDF vs ASCII Trajectories

The `netcdf` flag affects both performance and disk usage. NetCDF (`.nc`) is a binary format that is generally faster and more compact than ASCII (`.mdcrd`) [GMXMMPBSA/make_trajs.py:52-55]().

---

## Calculation-Specific Performance

### GBNSR6 Memory and I/O

GBNSR6 calculations are particularly resource-intensive because they require generating individual `inpcrd` files for every frame [GMXMMPBSA/main.py:398-407]().

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "GBNSR6_Resource_Flow"
        TRJ["Trajectory Frames"]
        INPCRD_GEN["make_trajs.py<br/>Write .inpcrd per frame"]
        DIR["_GMXMMPBSA_inpcrd_RANK/"]
        CALC["gbnsr6 executable"]
        JSON["amber_outputs.py<br/>mdout2json()"]
        
        TRJ --> INPCRD_GEN
        INPCRD_GEN --> DIR
        DIR --> CALC
        CALC --> JSON
    end
```

Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/main.py:365-412](), [GMXMMPBSA/calculation.py:404-411]()

### NMODE Convergence and Performance

NMODE calculations can be slow and may fail to converge. If the gradient in the minimization step is too high, `sander` may fail to produce valid entropy values, leading to `ValueError: could not convert string to float: '*************'` in the output parser [docs/Q&A/calculations.md:15-93]().

**Recommendations**:
- Ensure the trajectory is properly fitted and PBC is removed [docs/Q&A/calculations.md:43-88]().
- Check for "broken" structures in the input files [docs/Q&A/calculations.md:24-41]().
- Consider interaction entropy as a faster alternative [docs/Q&A/calculations.md:148-150]().

Sources: [docs/Q&A/calculations.md:15-150](), [GMXMMPBSA/amber_outputs.py:578-584]()

---

## Common Resource Issues and Solutions

### Large System Limitations
When calculating energy for very large groups, the energy value might exceed the 7-digit limit allowed by the `sander` output format, causing a `ValueError` [docs/Q&A/calculations.md:90-93]().

**Solutions**:
- Recompile `sander` with modified output formats (not recommended).
- Modify calculation parameters (solvent model, dielectric).
- Perform calculations on a sub-system [docs/Q&A/calculations.md:97-100]().

### PB Model Performance
High non-polar solvation energy values in PB models can occur due to the `EDISPER` term (`inp=2`). Using `inp=1` models non-polar solvation as a single term proportional to SASA, which is often faster and avoids imbalances between cavity and dispersion terms [docs/Q&A/calculations.md:103-146]().

### OS and GUI Issues
- **WSL**: No graphics drivers, so `gmx_MMPBSA_ana` cannot run [docs/Q&A/OS_issues.md:19-21]().
- **HPC**: GUI is disabled; use `-nogui` [docs/Q&A/OS_issues.md:29-33]().
- **Qt Plugins**: Reinstalling `libxcb-xinerama0` can fix plugin loading errors [docs/Q&A/OS_issues.md:35-46]().

Sources: [docs/Q&A/calculations.md:90-146](), [docs/Q&A/OS_issues.md:16-46]()

---

## Version Timeline and Major Releases

gmx_MMPBSA follows semantic versioning with major releases introducing breaking changes, minor releases adding features, and patch releases fixing bugs. The project has evolved through several significant milestones since its initial release.

```mermaid
graph TB
```

## Current Version Requirements

The latest version (v1.6.5) enforces specific dependency versions for stability and compatibility. Notably, Python 3.11 is now a strict requirement.

| Dependency | Version Requirement | Notes |
|------------|-------------------|-------|
| Python | 3.11 (strict) | Enforced in setup.py [docs/changelog.md:43-43]() |
| AmberTools | 20, 21, 22, or 23 | Provides calculation engines |
| GROMACS | All versions supported | Up to GROMACS 2023 [docs/changelog.md:84-84]() |
| mpi4py | Required for MPI | Used when `mpi_size > 1` [docs/changelog.md:116-116]() |
| ParmEd | Latest compatible | Topology conversion |

**Sources:** [docs/changelog.md:38-44](), [docs/changelog.md:84-84](), [docs/changelog.md:116-116]()

---

## Breaking Changes by Version

### Version 1.6.5 → Dependency Tightening (May 2024)
- **Python 3.11 Constraint**: The package now strictly requires Python 3.11 [docs/changelog.md:43-43]().
- **Installation**: A new installation script `scripts/conda_pip_install.sh` was introduced to manage environment complexities [docs/changelog.md:28-28]().

### Version 1.5.0 → Major Refactor (February 2022)
Version 1.5.0 introduced the most significant breaking changes, fundamentally reworking calculation and processing modules.

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "v1.4.x Input Entity"
        old1["protein_forcefield"]
        old2["ligand_forcefield"]
        old3["entropy = 1 or 2"]
        old4["entropy_seg"]
        old5["entropy_temp"]
    end
    
    subgraph "v1.5.0 Input Entity"
        new1["forcefields"]
        new2["qh_entropy"]
        new3["interaction_entropy"]
        new4["ie_segment"]
        new5["temperature"]
    end
    
    old1 -.replaced_by.-> new1
    old2 -.replaced_by.-> new1
    old3 -.split_into.-> new2
    old3 -.split_into.-> new3
    old4 -.renamed_to.-> new4
    old5 -.renamed_to.-> new5
```

#### Removed Variables
- `protein_forcefield` and `ligand_forcefield` → Replaced by a single `forcefields` variable [docs/compatibility.md:81-83]().
- `use_sander` → Removed; sander is the default engine [docs/compatibility.md:49-49]().

#### New Capabilities in v1.5.0
- **&general**: `c2_entropy` [docs/compatibility.md:26-26]().
- **&pb**: Extensive control with 18+ new variables like `smoothopt`, `iprob`, and `npbopt` for non-linear PB solvers [docs/compatibility.md:30-32]().
- **&rism**: Advanced 3D-RISM parameters including `mdiis_del` and `entropicDecomp` [docs/compatibility.md:34-37]().

**Sources:** [docs/compatibility.md:15-55](), [GMXMMPBSA/infofile.py:29-61]()

---

## Deprecated Features Tracking

The codebase maintains a mapping of old variables to new namelists for backward compatibility, though many were formally removed in v1.5.0.

| Variable | Deprecated In | Removed In | Replacement | Namelist |
|----------|--------------|------------|-------------|-------|
| `protein_forcefield` | v1.4.1 | v1.5.0 | `forcefields` | `&general` |
| `ligand_forcefield` | v1.4.1 | v1.5.0 | `forcefields` | `&general` |
| `entropy` | v1.4.2 | v1.5.0 | `qh_entropy` / `interaction_entropy` | `&general` |
| `entropy_seg` | v1.4.2 | v1.5.0 | `ie_segment` | `&general` |
| `entropy_temp` | v1.4.1 | v1.5.0 | `temperature` | `&general` |

**Internal Handling:**
The `InfoFile` class in `GMXMMPBSA/infofile.py` manages these transitions. It defines `nl_variables` to map old names to their respective namelists [GMXMMPBSA/infofile.py:29-61]() and tracks editable variables like `exp_ki` and `sys_name` [GMXMMPBSA/infofile.py:73-75]().

**Sources:** [docs/compatibility.md:101-121](), [GMXMMPBSA/infofile.py:29-80]()

---

## Migration Guide: 1.4.3 → 1.5.0

### Option 1: Update the Input File
The most robust method is to regenerate or update your `.in` file using the new syntax. v1.5.0 introduced a GROMACS-like format [docs/input_file.md:10-12]().

```bash
# Generate a template for the new format
gmx_MMPBSA --create_input all
```

### Option 2: Modify the Info File
For existing results, you can edit the `_GMXMMPBSA_info` file to make them compatible with `gmx_MMPBSA_ana` v1.5.0+.

```python
# Manually add missing metadata to _GMXMMPBSA_info
INPUT['general']['temperature'] = 298.15
INPUT['general']['sys_name'] = 'My_Complex'
INPUT['general']['exp_ki'] = 1.5
```

**Sources:** [docs/compatibility.md:140-162](), [GMXMMPBSA/infofile.py:97-101]()

---

## File Format Compatibility

### Binary Output (.mmxsa)
The binary format used for the analyzer was completely reworked in v1.5.0 and v1.5.6 [docs/changelog.md:140-140]().
- **v1.5.6**: Re-implementation of compact binary output file [docs/changelog.md:140-140]().
- **v1.6.0**: A copy of the old info file is created when rewriting output to preserve backward compatibility [docs/changelog.md:90-90]().

### Info File Evolution
The `InfoFile` class handles writing metadata so that post-processing can occur without re-supplying all command-line arguments [GMXMMPBSA/infofile.py:1-5]().
- **Editable Variables**: Users can alter `exp_ki`, `sys_name`, and `ie_segment` within the info file [GMXMMPBSA/infofile.py:73-75]().
- **Careful Variables**: `inp` (PB solver) is marked as "edit with care" [GMXMMPBSA/infofile.py:77-77]().

**Sources:** [GMXMMPBSA/infofile.py:63-113](), [docs/changelog.md:89-91]()

---

# Page: Changelog and Release Notes

# Changelog and Release Notes

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [GMXMMPBSA/__init__.py](GMXMMPBSA/__init__.py)
- [GMXMMPBSA/app.py](GMXMMPBSA/app.py)

- [docs/compatibility.md](docs/compatibility.md)
- [docs/gmx_MMPBSA_running.md](docs/gmx_MMPBSA_running.md)
- [docs/input_file.md](docs/input_file.md)
- [docs/news.json](docs/news.json)
- [setup.py](setup.py)

</details>



This page provides a comprehensive technical history of `gmx_MMPBSA` development. It details the evolution of the codebase from its initial release through version 1.6.5, highlighting major architectural shifts, API changes, and the integration of advanced solvation models and entropy methods.

## Overview of Development History

The development of `gmx_MMPBSA` has focused on bridging the gap between GROMACS trajectories and AMBER-based energy engines. Key milestones include the transition to a modular API in v1.5.x and the implementation of advanced numerical models like GBNSR6 in v1.6.x.

### Codebase Evolution Diagram
The following diagram illustrates the relationship between the core application modules and how they have evolved through various versions to handle data flow from GROMACS to final analysis.

**Title: gmx_MMPBSA Core Logic Flow and Module Evolution**
```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Input Processing"
        A["app.py (gmxmmpbsa)"] --> B["commandlineparser.py"]
        A --> C["input_parser.py"]
    end

    subgraph "Topology & Trajectory (make_*.py)"
        D["make_top.py"] -- "Generates AMBER prmtop" --> E["make_trajs.py"]
        E -- "Extracts frames via cpptraj" --> F["calculation.py"]
    end

    subgraph "Energy Engines (v1.6.0+)"
        F --> G["GB/PB Solvers"]
        F --> H["GBNSR6 (v1.6.0)"]
        F --> I["3D-RISM"]
    end

    subgraph "Output & Analysis"
        G & H & I --> J["amber_outputs.py"]
        J -- "Binary .mmxsa" --> K["analyzer/gui.py"]
        J -- "Text .dat/.csv" --> L["Final Results"]
    end

    C -.-> D
    B -.-> A
```
Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/app.py:40-113](), [GMXMMPBSA/__init__.py:24-26](), [docs/changelog.md:68-72]()

---

## v1.6.x Series: Advanced Models and Stability

The 1.6.x series introduced significant scientific capabilities, most notably the GBNSR6 model, and improved compatibility with modern GROMACS versions.

### v1.6.5 (Current Stable)
*   **CHARMM NMODE Support:** Experimental implementation of Normal Mode Analysis for systems using CHARMM topologies [docs/changelog.md:12-12]().
*   **Residue Selection:** Expanded support for histidine variants in residue selection logic [docs/changelog.md:13-13]().
*   **Bug Fixes:** 
    *   Stricter rules for detecting Lone Pair (LP) atoms to avoid energy inconsistencies [docs/changelog.md:16-16]().
    *   Fixed duplication in Interaction Entropy (IE) and C2 calculations [docs/changelog.md:19-19]().
    *   Resolved an issue where `ie_segment` updates in `gmx_MMPBSA_ana` were not correctly applied if the original input differed [docs/changelog.md:20-21]().

### v1.6.0
*   **GBNSR6 Model:** Full implementation of the GBNSR6 model, including Enthalpy and per-residue/pairwise decomposition [docs/changelog.md:69-72]().
*   **GROMACS 2023 Compatibility:** Updated internal calls to handle changes in GROMACS 2023 [docs/changelog.md:84-84]().
*   **Index File Logic:** Groups can now be defined by either number or name, with improved error tracking for missing groups [docs/changelog.md:74-75]().

Sources: [docs/changelog.md:7-46](), [docs/changelog.md:66-92]()

---

## v1.5.x Series: The API and Analyzer Revolution

Version 1.5.0 marked a breaking change from the 1.4.x series, introducing a completely reworked Analyzer (`gmx_MMPBSA_ana`) and a robust API for programmatic access.

### Architectural Changes in v1.5.0
The application was restructured to separate data processing from visualization. The introduction of the `.mmxsa` binary format allowed for faster data loading in the GUI [docs/changelog.md:140-140]().

**Title: Analyzer Data Flow and API Integration**
```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Data Provider (API)"
        A["API.py"] -- "Fetch Enthalpy" --> B["EnergyVector"]
        A -- "Fetch Entropy" --> C["EntropyVector"]
        A -- "Fetch Decomp" --> D["DecompData"]
    end

    subgraph "GUI (gmx_MMPBSA_ana)"
        E["analyzer/gui.py"] --> F["Multiprocessing Loader"]
        F --> G["DataTree View"]
        G --> H["Matplotlib Charts"]
    end

    B & C & D --> F
```
Sources: [docs/changelog.md:150-155](), [docs/changelog.md:188-196](), [GMXMMPBSA/app.py:123-151]()

### Key Additions in 1.5.x
*   **Multiprocessing:** Added to `gmx_MMPBSA_ana` to prevent GUI freezing during large dataset loads [docs/changelog.md:158-159]().
*   **Correlation Analysis:** New module for comparing predicted $\Delta G$ with experimental $K_i$ values, including regression plots [docs/changelog.md:163-174]().
*   **C2 Entropy:** Introduced as a new entropy approximation method [docs/compatibility.md:52-55]().
*   **Input Creation:** Added the `--create_input` flag to generate template input files [docs/input_file.md:30-36]().

Sources: [docs/changelog.md:144-204](), [docs/input_file.md:62-62]()

---

## v1.4.x Series: Refinement and MPI Stability

The 1.4.x series focused on stabilizing parallel execution and refining the input file format.

### Significant Changes
*   **MPI Integration:** Fixed inconsistencies when running with `mpirun`. The application now uses `mpi4py` when `mpi_size > 1`, otherwise falling back to a `fake_MPI` implementation for serial runs [docs/changelog.md:116-117](), [GMXMMPBSA/app.py:53-55]().
*   **Variable Renaming:** Standardized many input variables (e.g., `entropy = 1` became `qh_entropy`, `protein_forcefield` and `ligand_forcefield` were merged into `forcefields`) [docs/compatibility.md:68-88]().
*   **System Naming:** Introduced `sys_name` in the `&general` namelist to allow better organization of multi-system projects [docs/input_file.md:120-129]().

Sources: [docs/compatibility.md:65-121](), [GMXMMPBSA/app.py:40-57](), [docs/gmx_MMPBSA_running.md:79-81]()

---

## Summary of Breaking Changes and Migrations

| Version | Change Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1.5.0** | **Breaking** | Completely reworked `gmx_MMPBSA_ana`; incompatible with old `.info` files [docs/compatibility.md:16-17](). |
| **1.5.0** | **Removed** | `protein_forcefield`, `ligand_forcefield`, and `use_sander` variables removed [docs/compatibility.md:47-49](). |
| **1.4.2** | **Deprecated** | `entropy` variable deprecated in favor of `qh_entropy` or `interaction_entropy` [docs/compatibility.md:102-104](). |
| **1.4.0** | **CLI Change** | `gmx_MMPBSA_ana` changed `-p` option to `-f` [docs/compatibility.md:126-127](). |

### Variable Mapping for Migration
Users migrating from older versions should update their `mmpbsa.in` files as follows:
*   `entropy = 1` $\rightarrow$ `qh_entropy = 1` [docs/compatibility.md:69-70]()
*   `entropy = 2` $\rightarrow$ `interaction_entropy = 1` [docs/compatibility.md:73-74]()
*   `entropy_temp` $\rightarrow$ `temperature` [docs/compatibility.md:85-86]()
*   `entropy_seg` $\rightarrow$ `ie_segment` [docs/compatibility.md:77-78]()

Sources: [docs/compatibility.md:65-121](), [docs/input_file.md:145-149]()

---

## Technical Environment Requirements

As of v1.6.5, the software has strict dependency requirements to ensure stability with AmberTools and GROMACS.

*   **Python:** Exactly 3.11 [setup.py:26-27]().
*   **Core Libraries:** 
    *   `numpy==1.26.4` [setup.py:50-50]()
    *   `pandas==1.5.3` [setup.py:50-50]()
    *   `parmed>=4.2.2` [setup.py:54-54]()
    *   `mpi4py==4.0.1` [setup.py:53-53]()

Sources: [setup.py:26-61](), [docs/changelog.md:38-43]()

# Page: Migration Guides

# Migration Guides

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [GMXMMPBSA/infofile.py](GMXMMPBSA/infofile.py)
- [docs/changelog.md](docs/changelog.md)
- [docs/compatibility.md](docs/compatibility.md)
- [docs/gmx_MMPBSA_running.md](docs/gmx_MMPBSA_running.md)
- [docs/input_file.md](docs/input_file.md)
- [docs/news.json](docs/news.json)

</details>



This page provides technical documentation for migrating between major versions of `gmx_MMPBSA`. It covers breaking changes in input variables, architectural shifts, and data format updates.

## Purpose and Scope

As `gmx_MMPBSA` has evolved from its initial release, several major versions (1.4.x, 1.5.x, 1.6.x) have introduced architectural changes to improve performance, accuracy, and feature sets. This guide assists users and developers in updating their workflows and input files to maintain compatibility with the latest stable releases.

## 1. Migration from 1.5.x to 1.6.x

The transition to version 1.6.x focuses on expanding solvation models (GBNSR6) and refining existing entropy and topology handling.

### Key Changes
*   **GBNSR6 Support:** Introduction of the `&gbnsr6` namelist for advanced Generalized Born calculations [docs/input_file.md:18-18]().
*   **GROMACS 2023 Compatibility:** Updates to handle changes in GROMACS trajectory and topology formats [docs/changelog.md:84-84]().
*   **Stricter Atom Detection:** Enhanced rules for detecting Lone Pair (LP) atoms in CHARMM force fields [docs/changelog.md:16-16]().
*   **Python Requirement:** Version 1.6.5 restricts the Python environment to 3.11 for stability [docs/changelog.md:43-43]().

### Variable Mapping (1.5.x to 1.6.x)
| Old Variable (1.5.x) | New Variable (1.6.x) | Context |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| N/A | `&gbnsr6` namelist | New solvation model [docs/input_file.md:18-18]() |
| `saopt` | *Removed* | Removed from PB/LPH documentation [docs/changelog.md:31-31]() |
| `inp` | `inp = 1` (Default) | Now defaults to 1 for PB calculations [docs/changelog.md:91-91]() |

Sources: [docs/input_file.md:18-18](), [docs/changelog.md:16-91]()

---

## 2. Migration from 1.4.x to 1.5.x

Version 1.5.0 represented a major overhaul of the codebase, introducing significant breaking changes in both the core application and the analyzer.

### Architectural Shift: Parallelism and API
In version 1.5.0, the `gmx_MMPBSA_ana` tool was completely reworked to include multiprocessing and multithreading [docs/changelog.md:158-158](). A new programmatic API was introduced to allow data access via `MMPBSA_API` [docs/changelog.md:150-156]().

### Variable Rework and Deprecations
Many variables in the `&general` namelist were renamed to be more descriptive or to consolidate functionality.

| 1.4.x Variable | 1.5.x Variable | Namelist |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `entropy = 1` | `qh_entropy` | `&general` |
| `entropy = 2` | `interaction_entropy` | `&general` |
| `entropy_seg` | `ie_segment` | `&general` |
| `entropy_temp` | `temperature` | `&general` |
| `protein_forcefield` | `forcefields` | `&general` |
| `ligand_forcefield` | `forcefields` | `&general` |
| `use_sander` | *Removed* | N/A |

Sources: [docs/compatibility.md:15-121](), [GMXMMPBSA/infofile.py:29-61]()

### Logic Flow for Legacy Variable Support
The `InfoFile` class in `GMXMMPBSA/infofile.py` maintains a mapping of variables to their respective namelists to provide backward compatibility where possible, though direct use of old variables in `mmpbsa.in` is discouraged.

**Variable to Namelist Mapping Logic**
`nl_variables` dictionary in `infofile.py` maps legacy and current keys to their parent namelists [GMXMMPBSA/infofile.py:29-61]().

**Data Flow: Legacy Variable Resolution**
```mermaid
graph TD
    A["Input File (mmpbsa.in)"] --> B{"v1.5+ Parser"}
    B -- "New Variables" --> C["Process Calculation"]
    B -- "Legacy Variables" --> D{"infofile.py mapping"}
    D --> E["Map to &general/&gb/&pb"]
    E --> F["Warning Issued"]
    F --> C
    C --> G["_GMXMMPBSA_info Generated"]
```
Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/infofile.py:29-61](), [docs/compatibility.md:140-162]()

---

## 3. Data Format Changes

### Info File Migration
The `_GMXMMPBSA_info` file (managed by `InfoFile` class) changed its internal structure. In version 1.6.0, a copy of the old info file is created when rewriting output to prevent data loss [docs/changelog.md:89-90]().

### Compact Binary Format
Version 1.5.6 introduced a re-implementation of the compact binary output file (`.mmxsa`) to optimize storage for large trajectories [docs/changelog.md:140-140](). Version 1.5.0+ of `gmx_MMPBSA_ana` is incompatible with binary files generated by versions `< 1.5.2` [docs/changelog.md:186-186]().

### Logic: Info File Variable Writing
The `InfoFile.write_info` method distinguishes between editable and non-editable variables to prevent users from corrupting the state of a calculation during post-processing.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Code Entity Space: GMXMMPBSA/infofile.py"
    IF["Class: InfoFile"]
    EV["EDITABLE_INFO_VARS"]
    WC["EDIT_WITH_CARE_VARS"]
    WI["Function: write_info()"]
    end

    subgraph "Natural Language Space: Migration Actions"
    U1["User modifies exp_ki"]
    U2["User modifies sys_name"]
    U3["User attempts to modify internal masks"]
    end

    U1 --> EV
    U2 --> EV
    U3 -- "Restricted" --> WC
    EV --> WI
    WC --> WI
    WI --> OUT["_GMXMMPBSA_info file"]
```
Sources: [GMXMMPBSA/infofile.py:72-117](), [docs/compatibility.md:140-162]()

---

## 4. Summary of Major Calculation Changes

| Feature | 1.4.x | 1.5.x | 1.6.x |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Solvation** | GB/PB/RISM | + Non-linear PB | + GBNSR6 |
| **Entropy** | QH/IE | + C2 Entropy | + CHARMM NMODE |
| **Parallelism** | MPI (Experimental) | MPI (Stable/Default) | MPI + Optimized API |
| **Force Fields** | AMBER | + CHARMM/OPLS | + Enhanced LPH support |

### Implementation Note on MPI
Since version 1.5.7, the application automatically uses `mpi4py` if `mpi_size > 1`, otherwise falling back to `fake_MPI`. The explicit "MPI" flag used in older versions is no longer required [docs/changelog.md:116-117]().

Sources: [docs/changelog.md:7-117](), [docs/compatibility.md:52-59](), [docs/gmx_MMPBSA_running.md:79-81]()

---

This glossary defines technical terms, abbreviations, and domain-specific concepts used within the `gmx_MMPBSA` codebase.

## Core Concepts and Abbreviations

### MM/PBSA (Molecular Mechanics / Poisson-Boltzmann Surface Area)
A method used to estimate the binding free energy of small molecules to biological macromolecules. It combines molecular mechanics energies with continuum solvation models.
*   **Implementation:** Orchestrated by the `MMPBSA_App` class which manages the data flow from GROMACS files to energy calculations [GMXMMPBSA/main.py:65-110]().

### GB (Generalized Born)
A computationally efficient model used to estimate the electrostatic contribution to solvation free energy.
*   **Code Reference:** Handled by `GBout` for output parsing [GMXMMPBSA/amber_outputs.py:32-35]() and `EnergyCalculation` for execution [GMXMMPBSA/calculation.py:36-38]().

### PB (Poisson-Boltzmann)
A more rigorous (and computationally expensive) method for calculating electrostatic solvation energy by solving the Poisson-Boltzmann equation.
*   **Code Reference:** Handled by `PBout` [GMXMMPBSA/amber_outputs.py:32-35]() and `PBEnergyCalculation` [GMXMMPBSA/calculation.py:36-38]().

### Decomposition Analysis
A method to break down the total binding free energy into contributions from individual residues (per-residue) or pairs of residues (pairwise).
*   **Implementation:** Controlled by the `idecomp` parameter. Modes 1-4 define different levels of interaction inclusion (e.g., 1-4 interactions) [GMXMMPBSA/amber_outputs.py:37-41]().

## Code-Specific Terminology

### EnergyVector
A specialized subclass of `numpy.ndarray` used throughout the codebase to store and manipulate per-frame energy data. It includes built-in methods for statistical analysis (SD, SEM) and uncertainty propagation.
*   **Definition:** `class EnergyVector(np.ndarray)` [GMXMMPBSA/utils.py:52-151]().
*   **Key Methods:** `stdev()`, `sem()`, `corr_add()` (for correlated uncertainty), and `avg()` [GMXMMPBSA/utils.py:86-107]().

### Namelist
A structure mimicking Fortran namelists used in AMBER. It groups variables (like `&general`, `&gb`, `&pb`) for organized input file parsing.
*   **Definition:** `class Namelist(object)` [GMXMMPBSA/input_parser.py:106-121]().
*   **Usage:** Variables are added via `addVariable` [GMXMMPBSA/input_parser.py:143-149]().

### ST vs MT (Single-Trajectory vs Multi-Trajectory)
*   **ST (Single-Trajectory):** Binding energy is calculated using a single trajectory of the complex. Receptor and Ligand coordinates are extracted from this trajectory.
*   **MT (Multi-Trajectory):** Uses three separate trajectories (Complex, Receptor, Ligand). This is more rigorous but requires significantly more simulation time.
*   **Validation:** The `MMPBSA_App` checks if trajectory lengths match for MT protocols [GMXMMPBSA/main.py:143-146]().

## Data Flow and Entities

The following diagram illustrates the relationship between GROMACS input entities and the internal code classes that process them.

### Diagram: Input to Code Entity Mapping
```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Natural Language Space"
        GMX_FILES["GROMACS Files (.tpr, .xtc)"]
        INPUT_IN["Input Config (mmpbsa.in)"]
        TOP_CONV["Topology Conversion"]
    end

    subgraph "Code Entity Space"
        APP["MMPBSA_App (main.py)"]
        IP["input_file (input_parser.py)"]
        CMT["CheckMakeTop (make_top.py)"]
        EV["EnergyVector (utils.py)"]
        CALC["CalculationList (calculation.py)"]
    end

    GMX_FILES -->|"Processed by"| CMT
    INPUT_IN -->|"Parsed by"| IP
    IP -->|"Initializes"| APP
    CMT -->|"Generates Amber Topologies"| APP
    APP -->|"Triggers"| CALC
    CALC -->|"Produces Data"| EV
```
**Sources:** [GMXMMPBSA/main.py:65-110](), [GMXMMPBSA/make_top.py:76-112](), [GMXMMPBSA/input_parser.py:106-121](), [GMXMMPBSA/utils.py:52-63]().

## Solvation Models and Entropy Terms

| Term | Description | Code Entity |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **GGB** | Gas-phase energy (Bond, Angle, Dihedral, VDW, EEL) | `AmberOutput['GGAS']` [GMXMMPBSA/amber_outputs.py:89-91]() |
| **GSOLV** | Solvation free energy (Polar + Non-polar) | `AmberOutput['GSOLV']` [GMXMMPBSA/amber_outputs.py:91]() |
| **IE** | Interaction Entropy (efficient entropy approximation) | `IEout` [GMXMMPBSA/amber_outputs.py:32-35]() |
| **NMODE** | Normal Mode Analysis (rigorous vibrational entropy) | `NmodeCalc` [GMXMMPBSA/calculation.py:36-38]() |
| **QH** | Quasi-Harmonic Entropy | `QuasiHarmCalc` [GMXMMPBSA/calculation.py:36-38]() |

## Analyzer (GUI) Components

The `gmx_MMPBSA_ana` application uses a Model-View-Controller style architecture.

### Diagram: GUI Architecture
```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "UI Layer"
        GANA["GMX_MMPBSA_ANA (gui.py)"]
        TREE["QTreeWidget (Data Tree)"]
        CHART["ChartsBase (plots.py)"]
    end

    subgraph "Data Layer"
        API["MMPBSA_API (API.py)"]
        MMXSA[".mmxsa file (Binary Data)"]
        EV_ANA["EnergyVector"]
    end

    GANA -->|"Uses"| TREE
    TREE -->|"Calls"| API
    API -->|"Loads"| MMXSA
    API -->|"Returns"| EV_ANA
    GANA -->|"Visualizes in"| CHART
```
**Sources:** [GMXMMPBSA/analyzer/gui.py:44-71](), [GMXMMPBSA/API.py:33-46](), [GMXMMPBSA/analyzer/plots.py:122-135](), [GMXMMPBSA/analyzer/customitem.py:104-140]().

### Key GUI Terms
*   **mmxsa:** A binary file format (pickled Python object) containing all results and metadata required for visualization [GMXMMPBSA/output_file.py:48-51]().
*   **CustomItem:** A specialized `QTreeWidgetItem` that represents a specific calculation result (e.g., GB or PB) and holds references to its plot windows [GMXMMPBSA/analyzer/customitem.py:104-132]().
*   **ParameterTree:** A GUI component for adjusting chart settings like colors, themes, and font sizes [GMXMMPBSA/analyzer/gui.py:137-140]().
